p:NGA: The Central Bank of Nigeria issues the naira (NGN). Its exposure score is 41 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed; that is more exposed than 84% of the 194 places with a figure. Of six documented cases, the main ones involve former governor Godwin Emefiele, whom the EFCC (Nigeria's anti-corruption agency) charged in 2024 over banknote printing and foreign exchange allocations. He pleaded not guilty to a separate 20-count charge, and none of these is a verdict. President Tinubu suspended him on 9 June 2023, and President Jonathan suspended governor Sanusi in February 2014. A swap line, an agreement to borrow another central bank's currency, links it to China: CNY 15 billion against NGN 3.28 trillion, dated 27 December 2024.
p:IDN: Bank Indonesia is the central bank of Indonesia and issues the rupiah. The country scores 32 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In October 2011 Securency and Note Printing Australia, subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in an Australian court to bribing foreign officials to win Indonesia's banknote business in 1999 to 2001. Governor Syahril was released in December 2000 after six months in detention, while facing charges over the 546 billion rupiah Bank Bali scandal; a court sentenced him to three years in 2002, but in 2004 the Supreme Court acquitted him on all charges. In October 2008 the Corruption Court sentenced former governor Burhanuddin Abdullah to five years for approving 100 billion rupiah of the bank's funds in 2003 to pay officials' legal fees and bribe legislators over an amendment to the bank's law. In July 2014 the anti-corruption court sentenced Budi Mulya to 10 years over a 689.39 billion rupiah loan to Bank Century, finding he had taken a one billion rupiah loan from its owner, Robert Tantular. In August 2025 the anti-corruption commission, the KPK, named two members of the House as suspects over alleged misuse of corporate social responsibility money from the bank; that is unproven.
p:PHL: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas issues the Philippine peso. The country scores 36 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In 2005 its internal audit found 5.955 million pesos missing from the Bacolod City branch, and the Ombudsman, the body that investigates officials, found the manager guilty of dishonesty and dismissed him. An examiner who had audited the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga took 103,500 pesos in fees from it through another firm; the anti-graft court, the Sandiganbayan, upheld his conviction, with six to seven years in prison. A former supervision officer took a loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba in 2006; the Ombudsman cleared him in 2011, but the Supreme Court reversed that and ordered charges, which are unproven. A 2013 complaint says former governor Amando Tetangco Jr and Monetary Board members gave Allied Bank an undue advantage in its merger with Philippine National Bank, and it was still pending in September 2025. A January 2021 complaint against Governor Benjamin Diokno and six officials over a 1.75-billion-peso identity card contract to AllCard International is also an allegation only. Four staff were dismissed in July 2024 for falsifying attendance records, and in August 2025 two supervisors drew the maximum penalties. In December 2016 President Rodrigo Duterte told Tetangco "I will give you a whack" and threatened charges against the Anti-Money Laundering Council he chaired.
p:BRA: Brazil's money is the real, and its central bank is the Central Bank of Brazil. It scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. One case is recorded and nothing is proven: on 3 October 2019 the Federal Police and Sao Paulo federal prosecutors opened Operation Estrela Cadente into leaks of the bank's interest-rate decisions in 2010, 2011 and 2012, said to have benefited a fund run by the bank BTG Pactual; it remains under investigation and the details are under court seal. On 21 June 2024 President Lula called bank president Roberto Campos Neto his political and ideological adversary and said Brazil would return to normality once he could replace him. Three leaders moved between the bank and private finance: Henrique Meirelles, president from 2003 to 2010, held posts at BankBoston and Lazard Americas; Ilan Goldfajn, governor from May 2016 to February 2019, at Itau Unibanco and Credit Suisse Brazil; and Campos Neto came from Santander and was to join the bank Nubank as vice chairman on 1 July 2025, after a six-month cooling-off period required by law.
p:LUX: Luxembourg uses the euro, so the Central Bank of Luxembourg does the country's central banking while the European Central Bank (ECB) sets interest rates for the 21 euro countries. Both cases on file belong to the ECB. The European Ombudsman ruled it maladministration for ECB president Mario Draghi to stay in the Group of Thirty, a forum that mixes central bankers with private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend his membership; the ECB declined and he did not. In May 2015 a speech by Cœuré to a private London event was published only the next morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. The bank's assets come to 268.1 percent of yearly national output. Luxembourg scores 20 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:FIN: Finland uses the euro, so the Bank of Finland does not set interest rates on its own; the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries that use the currency. Nothing is recorded against the Finnish bank itself, and both documented cases sit at the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 in ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum of central bankers and private financiers, and in January 2018 recommended he suspend it; the ECB declined and he did not. In 2015 a speech by board member Benoit Coeure saying the ECB would front-load asset purchases was published only the morning after he gave it at a private evening event in London, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error, and Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. PricewaterhouseCoopers has been recommended as the Bank's external auditor for the years 2026 to 2031. Finland scores 17 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, less exposed than 98 percent of the 194 places measured.
p:ZAF: South Africa's money, the rand, is issued by the South African Reserve Bank, which scores 35 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, 100 being fully exposed. It has private shareholders: 2,000,000 shares held by just over 800 holders, none allowed more than 10,000 shares, with votes only for South African residents, one per 200 shares, and no shareholder role in policy. A reported shareholder list from 30 June 2022 names the South African Mutual Life Assurance Society at 20,000 shares and the SA Police Widows' and Orphans' Fund at 10,520, above the legal limit. An Economic Freedom Fighters bill to have the state buy them out reached parliament's Standing Committee on Finance; at hearings on 2 July 2025 the National Treasury called it a forced takeover. In June 2017 the Public Protector ordered Absa to repay 1.125 billion rand for an apartheid-era Reserve Bank loan to Bankorp; on 16 February 2018 the Pretoria High Court set that report aside and ordered the Public Protector to pay part of the bank's costs personally. Gill Marcus went from chairing Absa Group to governor in November 2009; former governor Tito Mboweni became a Goldman Sachs adviser in 2010 and again in 2022.
p:LBN: Banque du Liban issues Lebanon's currency, the Lebanese pound (LBP). The map scores its exposure at 43 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed; the weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it (66). Its law gives it 0.437 of 1 on Romelli's independence rules (147 of 155), where 0 means the government holds the power. The map lists 6 cases. A 2023 forensic audit by Alvarez & Marsal found its foreign-currency position went from a $7.2 billion surplus at end-2015 to a $50.7 billion deficit at end-2020. Former governor Riad Salameh, in office for three decades until 2023, was indicted in January 2026 by Beirut's indictment chamber on charges including embezzlement, forgery and illicit enrichment, accused of taking $44.8 million from a bank consultancy account. He denies wrongdoing. French prosecutors issued an arrest warrant in May 2023 over alleged laundering of $330 million, and Germany issued a second. He is also under investigation over allegations that more than $300 million went through Forry Associates, a company controlled by his brother Raja. The bank holds 286.8 tonnes of gold, 74.5% of its reserves.
p:BEL: Belgium uses the euro, and the European Central Bank sets monetary policy for all 21 countries that use it. The National Bank of Belgium is the country's own central bank. Its 400,000 shares are split evenly: the Belgian State holds 200,000 registered shares that cannot be transferred, a stake fixed by law since 1948, and the other 200,000 trade on the Euronext Brussels stock exchange, with no other holder of 5 percent or more of the voting rights known to the Bank. Both documented cases sit at the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 and in January 2018 recommended that ECB president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers; the ECB declined and he did not. In 2015 a speech by board member Benoit Coeure on asset purchases was published only the morning after he gave it at a private London event, which the ECB called an internal procedure error, and Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. Belgium scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:KEN: The Central Bank of Kenya is the country's central bank and issues its money. Three cases are on file. In the Goldenberg scandal, the government paid cash subsidies for fictitious gold and diamond exports under President Daniel arap Moi. In March 2006 prosecutors indicted five people, including former governor Kotut and former deputy governor Riungu. They are charged, which is unproven. On 23 March 2006 governor Andrew Mullei was charged with four counts of abuse of office, including hiring his son as a consultant. He denied awarding Sh9 million in contracts irregularly, and no court outcome was found. From 2015 to 2018, Kenya's anti-corruption commission investigated current and former officials over the collapse of Imperial Bank, whose directors said bank officers helped embezzle Sh34 billion. That is under investigation and unproven. Kenya scores 37 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:ARG: Argentina's money is the peso, issued by the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic. It scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. In January 2010 the government called on governor Martin Redrado to resign after he refused to back a decree releasing 6.6 billion dollars of reserves, then fired him; the courts suspended both decrees and he resigned that month, with the reserves frozen and a court holding that Congress had to approve their use. Fifteen people, among them Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner and economy minister Axel Kicillof, were tried over its 2015 dollar-futures sales; the Federal Court of Criminal Cassation dismissed the case against all of them on 13 April 2021. In May 2023, an election year, it advanced another 140 billion pesos to the Treasury, using 99.2% of the limit agreed with the IMF. On 17 April 2026 La Nacion reported the bank is examining at least 900 million dollars bought at the official rate in 2022 and 2023 that allegedly reached the parallel market; the firms deny it and nothing is proven. In July 2026 President Javier Milei announced a bill to bar the bank from funding the state.
p:MEX: Mexico's money is the Mexican peso, and its central bank is the Bank of Mexico, known as Banxico. Mexico scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. On 23 March 2022 President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador announced the bank's unanimous rate rise, from 6 to 6.5 per cent, before the bank published it; on 25 March he said finance minister Rogelio Ramirez de la O, who sits in on board meetings, had told him the evening before, and he apologised to the governor and accepted that the Bank of Mexico law had been violated. A deputy governor called it an error rather than a leak. People also move between the bank and private finance: Agustin Carstens came from deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund to be governor from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2015, and former governor Guillermo Ortiz became chairman of BTG Pactual's Mexico business from 1 January 2016.
p:IND: India's money is the rupee, and its central bank is the Reserve Bank of India. It scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. One case is recorded and it is unproven: in December 2016, while 500 and 1,000 rupee notes were being withdrawn from circulation, the Central Bureau of Investigation arrested bank official K. Michael in Bangalore, accusing him of converting 15 million rupees of withdrawn notes into 100 rupee notes without legal documentation, with a state bank employee. On 10 December 2018 governor Urjit Patel resigned, saying only that it was for personal reasons; media reports said he was annoyed by repeated government attempts to influence policy. In September 2010 the banknote paper supplier De La Rue said some employees had deliberately falsified paper test certificates, and supply to the Reserve Bank was reportedly suspended afterwards. Three leaders came from elsewhere: Duvvuri Subbarao, governor from 2008 to 2013, was a lead economist at the World Bank; Raghuram Rajan was the International Monetary Fund's chief economist before his appointment in 2013; and Patel arrived as deputy governor in January 2013 from the Fund and Reliance Industries.
p:EST: Estonia uses the euro, so the European Central Bank, not the Bank of Estonia, sets interest rates, for all 21 European Union countries on the euro. The one Estonian case ended in acquittal. On 5 March 1999 the Tallinn City Court found Siim Kallas, a former head of the bank, and Kaju not guilty of abuse of power and of submitting false information over the loss of 10 million US dollars from the North Estonian Bank; prosecutor Jaan Naaber appealed ten days later. Another case concerns the European Central Bank, where the European Ombudsman found maladministration and recommended in January 2018 that President Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives; the bank declined and he did not. Seven career moves between that bank and private finance are recorded, none an accusation. Estonia scores 18 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:MLT: Malta uses the euro, with interest rates set by the European Central Bank (ECB). Its own case concerns governor Scicluna, previously the country's finance minister. On 29 May 2024 he pleaded not guilty to fraud and other financial crimes over the government's handling of a private hospital contract, the Vitals concession, during his time as minister. He stepped aside as governor in July 2024 and was reinstated in July 2025 after the ECB was consulted and raised no objections; the charges remain unproven. The European Ombudsman also found maladministration over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, and the ECB would not act on it. Malta scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:JPN: The Bank of Japan issues the yen and has capital of 100 million yen, of which the government holds 55 percent and private investors 45 percent through subscription certificates traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Those holders have no say in running it, and the bank does not name them. One case is on file: in June 2006 governor Fukui apologised and took a 30 percent pay cut for six months after disclosing that he had kept a 10 million yen investment, made in 1999, in a fund run by Yoshiaki Murakami, who was arrested for insider trading; by then the stake was worth 22 million yen. The bank said he broke no law or internal rule, and he did not resign. Nine people have moved between its Policy Board and private finance, among them Atsushi Mizuno, who joined Credit Suisse the month after his term. Japan scores 36 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:BGR: Bulgaria switched to the euro on 1 January 2026, at 1.95583 lev to the euro, and the Bulgarian National Bank joined the Eurosystem, the group of national central banks that work with the European Central Bank; its governor now sits on the ECB's rate-setting council. Its own case is the collapse of Corporate Commercial Bank, or Corpbank, in June 2014. Prosecutors charged two former deputy governors in charge of supervision with failing to take legally required action against Corpbank from February 2010, allegedly to favour its shareholders. Gounev was charged in June 2014 and removed by court order that December, and Simeonov about ten months later; neither charge has been proven. Corpbank's majority owner was accused of embezzling 206 million leva, also unproven. Bulgaria scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:AUT: Austria's money is the euro, so its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank (ECB) for all 21 euro countries, with the Oesterreichische Nationalbank taking part in that system. Its banknote printing subsidiary, OeBS, paid kickbacks to win orders: a 20 percent overcharge to the central bank of Azerbaijan and 14 percent to Syria's, about 14 million euros in all. Seven defendants were convicted in October 2014, and after a retrial a Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended terms and Meyer 21 months suspended, while former deputy governor Duchatczek was acquitted. At the ECB, the European Ombudsman ruled in January 2018 that Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, was maladministration and asked him to drop it; the ECB declined. Austria scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:IRL: Ireland uses the euro, and the Central Bank of Ireland does not set interest rates; the European Central Bank does so for the 21 euro countries. Its own case ran from 2008 to 2009, when Neary, the financial regulator, said he would retire early over how the regulator had handled 87 million euros in secret directors' loans at Anglo Irish Bank. The loans came to light in January 2008, and an internal committee found the matter was not pursued, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing; Neary said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008. The European Ombudsman separately found maladministration over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, and the ECB declined to act. Ireland scores 22 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LTU: Lithuania uses the euro, so the Bank of Lithuania does not set interest rates itself; the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries that use the currency. The local case ran from 2011 to 2014 and ended in an acquittal. A central bank official who monitored the commercial bank Snoras was sacked in November 2011 and charged with letting Snoras keep information from the central bank's leadership, including on assets held in Swiss banks. A guilty verdict of March 2014 was annulled by a Vilnius court, which found no crime had been committed; that ruling can still be appealed to the Supreme Court. Two other cases sit at the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and the ECB declined its January 2018 recommendation that he suspend it. In 2015 a speech on asset purchases was published only the morning after a private London event. Lithuania scores 21 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:HRV: Croatia uses the euro, and the European Central Bank sets monetary policy for it along with 20 other countries. The Croatian National Bank is the country's own central bank. In January 2022, after media reports, the Zagreb prosecution and the financial market regulator HANFA opened inquiries into whether senior central bank officials had traded securities of the commercial banks they supervise using inside information. The central bank said its executives sold bank shares before the ban took effect and that trading bonds was not prohibited. Those inquiries remain open and nothing has been proven. Two further cases concern the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and the ECB declined its recommendation that he give it up; and in 2015 a speech on asset purchases was published only the morning after a private London event, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Croatia scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:SVK: Slovakia uses the euro, so the National Bank of Slovakia does not set interest rates; the European Central Bank does that for the 21 euro countries. Its own case ended in a conviction. On 29 May 2025 the Specialised Criminal Court found the sitting governor, Kažimír, guilty of paying a 48,000 euro bribe in 2017 and 2018, while he was finance minister, to the head of the tax office in connection with audits of private companies, and fined him 200,000 euros. He denied wrongdoing and said he would appeal; the offence predates his central bank post. The European Ombudsman separately found maladministration over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, and the ECB declined to act. Slovakia scores 25 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LVA: Latvia uses the euro, and its central bank, the Bank of Latvia, takes part in the European Central Bank, which sets monetary policy for the 21 countries using the currency. Former governor Ilmars Rimsevics was convicted of taking a bribe and other material inducements by the Riga District Court on 20 December 2023 and sentenced to six years in prison with a five-year ban on holding public office; about 25,000 euro and several properties were confiscated. He was tried alongside the businessman Maris Martinsons. Two further cases concern the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 and in January 2018 recommended that ECB president Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives; the ECB declined and he did not. In 2015 a speech on front-loading asset purchases, given at a private London event, was published only the next morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Latvia scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:SVN: Slovenia uses the euro, so its central bank, the Bank of Slovenia, does not set interest rates itself; the European Central Bank sets them for the 21 countries that use the euro. Slovenia scores 22 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, the 182nd of 194 places. The main local matter is the 2013 bank bailout, in which a 960 million euro bail-in, meaning losses forced on investors, hit about 100,000 junior bondholders and shareholders. Police investigators filed a second criminal complaint alleging abuse of office over it, after a 2016 attempt failed over procedural errors; the specialised prosecutor has asked the court to investigate, and nothing is proven. That inquiry included a search of the bank's premises on 6 July 2016, over which the European Central Bank's President wrote to Slovenia's prosecutor general and to the European Commission about information seized. Two findings concern the European Central Bank itself: that it leaked, on 18 May 2015, when Benoit Coeure told a private London event it would front-load asset purchases before the speech was published; and that the European Ombudsman found maladministration in January 2018 and recommended Mario Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and financiers, which the bank declined to do. Draghi came to central banking from Goldman Sachs International, and other board members arrived from or left for Lehman Brothers, Societe Generale, Lazard and BBVA.
p:MYS: Bank Negara Malaysia is the country's central bank and issues the ringgit. Malaysia scores 29 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two bribery cases are documented, both from banknote printing. In July 2011 the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission charged former Bank Negara official Mohamad Daud with taking two bribes of 50,000 ringgit in 2004 and 2005, over a 95 million ringgit contract for the five-ringgit polymer note won by Note Printing Australia. The Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted him on 6 December 2015 without calling his defence, and the Attorney-General withdrew the appeal in February 2016. In October 2011 Securency and Note Printing Australia, subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign officials to obtain banknote business with Malaysia's note-issuing authority between 2001 and 2003. No Malaysian official was named. Zeti Akhtar Aziz, governor for 16 years until 2016, became group chairman of the fund manager Permodalan Nasional Bhd.
p:HUN: Magyar Nemzeti Bank issues the forint (HUF), which floats within a de facto band of 5% against the euro. It is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. Its exposure score is 30 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed. Its independence in law is 0.876 of 1 on Romelli's 42 rules, where 1 means the bank holds the power. On 21 October 2026 former governor Matolcsy was detained on suspicion of economic fraud and use of a forged private document, according to his lawyer; this is under investigation and unproven. In March 2025 the State Audit Office reported mismanagement of public funds and losses of hundreds of billions of forints at MNB-controlled foundations and filed a criminal complaint. In June 2016 the Public Procurement Board fined six foundations 200,000 forints each. A swap line with China covers CNY 40 billion / HUF 1,900 billion.
p:GRC: Greece uses the euro, and rates are set by the European Central Bank. Unusually, the Bank of Greece is a listed company with 19,864,886 shares traded in Athens. The Greek State holds 1,774,088 of them, 8.93 percent, after taking over 1,309,210 shares from DEKA S.A. when that body was dissolved under a 2011 law. A social security fund, e-EFKA, is listed at 12.4402 percent as of 7 August 2020, but that figure comes from Wikipedia and is not confirmed in a bank filing. On 29 August 2019 Greek prosecutors dropped charges that governor Stournaras had taken bribes from the drug company Novartis while finance minister, together with charges against six other former senior officials. Greece scores 31 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:TUR: Türkiye's money is the Turkish lira, issued by the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, which scores 46 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. It has shareholders: at the end of 2025 the Ministry of Treasury and Finance held 55.12 percent, the state-owned Ziraat Bankası 19.22 percent and Mervak İç ve Dış Ticaret 5.12 percent. Four governors have been removed by presidential decree: Murat Cetinkaya in July 2019, after the bank held its rate at 24 percent; Murat Uysal on 7 November 2020, after the lira lost 30 percent of its value that year; Naci Agbal on 20 March 2021, four months in, after a rate rise; and Şahap Kavcıoğlu on 8 June 2023, having cut rates from 19 to 8.5 percent. His replacement, Hafize Gaye Erkan, came from Goldman Sachs and First Republic Bank. Government pressure was reported in 23 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, 21 in election periods. In October 2025 Istanbul prosecutors arrested former deputy governor Şener in an investigation into corruption and tender-rigging in two 2023 tenders at the Interbank Card Center, the payment network the bank majority-owns; that investigation is open and nothing is proven.
p:BGD: Bangladesh Bank is the country's central bank. It scores 41 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. On the night of 4 February 2016, attackers used its SWIFT access (the network banks use to send payments) to take money from its account at the New York Federal Reserve: 101 million dollars per The Daily Star, 81 million per Prothom Alo. A government inquiry's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted at involvement of central bank officials, but it was never published and no one had been punished as of 2019. Governor Atiur Rahman resigned on 15 March 2016 after the loss. In June 2025 the Anti-Corruption Commission began investigating him over alleged abuse of power and favouring loan defaulters; this is unproven. Former deputy governor SK Sur was arrested on 14 January 2025 and is charged, which is unproven. Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned on 9 August 2024, citing health reasons.
p:CYP: Cyprus uses the euro, so the Central Bank of Cyprus follows interest rates set by the European Central Bank for the 21 countries using it. Prosecutors charged former governor Christodoulos Christodoulou and five others with corruption, money laundering and abuse of office over a 1 million euro payment made in 2007 by a Greek businessman; on 31 July 2020 judges dismissed that case, ruling he should not have been tried twice. He said he was not bribed. In 2014 he pleaded guilty to six tax offences over the undeclared payment, from Focus Maritime Corporation, and was jailed for five months. He also faced 29 unproven charges over a payment said to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos and Marfin Investment Group taking control of Laiki Bank. Governor Panicos Demetriades resigned in March 2014 after the President of Cyprus said he would move to remove him.
p:NLD: The Netherlands uses the euro, whose monetary policy the European Central Bank sets for 21 member countries. De Nederlandsche Bank is the Dutch central bank within that system. In June 2010 the Scheltema committee, set up by finance minister Wouter Bos, reported that De Nederlandsche Bank had fallen seriously short as supervisor of DSB bank: it missed flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and was too patient afterwards, though the committee thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse. Two further cases concern the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 over president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum of financiers and central bankers, and in January 2018 recommended he suspend it; the ECB declined and he did not. In May 2015 a board member's speech on asset purchases was given at a private London event and published only the next morning. Wim Duisenberg came to the Dutch bank in 1981, becoming chairman in 1982, after three years at the International Monetary Fund and a seat on the board of Rabobank. EY audits the accounts. The Netherlands scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:FRA: France uses the euro, so the Bank of France does not set rates alone; the European Central Bank does that for the 21 euro countries. Jean-Claude Trichet, while governor, was charged with spreading false information and publishing inexact accounts of the state-owned bank Crédit Lyonnais for 1991 to mid-1993, and prosecutors asked for a 10-month suspended sentence. In June 2003 judges cleared him, finding he had only imprecise or incorrect information about the losses; Jacques de Larosière, a governor of that period, was accused alongside him. François Villeroy de Galhau became governor on 1 November 2015 after serving as chief operating officer of BNP Paribas, a career move and not wrongdoing. The bank holds 2,437 tonnes of gold and prints its own banknotes at Chamalières. France scores 21 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LKA: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka issues the rupee (LKR). It scores 34 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. Its legal independence scores 0.75 of 1 on one index (1 means the bank holds the power). Two cases are recorded. On 14 November 2023 a majority of a five-judge Supreme Court bench ruled that the three Rajapaksa brothers, former governors Cabraal and Lakshman, and others violated the public trust. In June 2019 the Attorney General filed a 23-count indictment against former governor Arjuna Mahendran and nine others over a February 2015 treasury bond auction; these are charges, not findings. President Maithripala Sirisena said in 2017 that he personally removed Mahendran. The bank has four swap lines (agreements to borrow another central bank's currency), with China and India.
p:ITA: The Bank of Italy is Italy's central bank, and because Italy uses the euro its interest rates are set by the European Central Bank. The Bank is owned by Italian banks, insurers, social security bodies, pension funds and banking foundations, which hold its capital of 7.5 billion euro as 300,000 quotas of 25,000 euro each. There were 173 holders on 30 April 2026, none allowed more than 5 percent since 1 January 2022, up from 3 percent under Law 5/2014; quotas above the cap carry no voting or economic rights. UniCredit sits at the cap with 15,000 quotas, the pension funds INARCASSA, ENPAM and Cassa Forense hold 14,800 each, Intesa Sanpaolo 14,736, CNPADC 11,000 and BPER Banca 9,765. Former governor Antonio Fazio was sentenced by a Milan court on 28 May 2011 to four years and a 1.5 million euro fine for market rigging in the 2005 attempt by Banca Popolare di Lodi to take over Antonveneta, prosecutors arguing he had favoured Gianpiero Fiorani's bank over ABN Amro by speeding some authorisations and slowing others; the appeal court cut the sentence to two years and six months on 28 May 2012 and the Court of Cassation made the conviction final on 28 November 2012. In a separate case over Unipol's attempted takeover of BNL he was sentenced to three and a half years in October 2011, then acquitted along with 12 other defendants on 30 May 2012. Two more cases sit at the European Central Bank, over Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty and a 2015 speech published a day late. Deloitte audits the accounts. Italy scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:POL: Poland's money is the zloty, issued by the National Bank of Poland, which scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Six cases are recorded. In the ArtB cheque affair of 1991, bank president Grzegorz Wojtowicz was charged with unintentionally causing about 72 billion old zloty of losses, and was acquitted. In February 2009 the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau detained eight people over the head of the bank's computing division, accused of taking at least 350,000 zloty in bribes to rig tenders from 2001 to 2008; the businessmen were charged, and nothing is proven. Warsaw prosecutors are investigating a leak from a closed Monetary Policy Council meeting on 8 September 2023, and seized documents at the bank's head office in June 2025. In March 2024 ruling-coalition members of parliament moved to try bank president Adam Glapinski before the State Tribunal, which hears cases against senior officials, on eight charges, among them bond purchases in 2020 and 2021 said to have indirectly financed the budget deficit by at least 144 billion zloty. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal ruled the enabling law unconstitutional and dismissed the case. A Sejm committee upheld all eight charges in a report on 9 October 2026, with the full vote expected in late November 2026; the bank calls them groundless and nothing is proven.
p:AUS: The Reserve Bank of Australia issues the Australian dollar. It scores 23 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and no government pressure on it was reported in any of the 37 quarters surveyed from 2010 to 2018. Its one documented case came out of its own banknote businesses: in October 2011 the subsidiaries Securency and Note Printing Australia pleaded guilty to conspiring to bribe foreign officials to win banknote work from the note-issuing authorities of Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Nepal. They paid proceeds-of-crime penalties of 19.8 million and 1.86 million Australian dollars and fines of 480,000 and 450,000 Australian dollars. Securency's former chief financial officer got a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting in 2012, the agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence in 2013. Three governors went into private finance on leaving: Ian Macfarlane to the ANZ board in 2007, Glenn Stevens to Macquarie Group in 2017 and Philip Lowe to Barrenjoey in 2024.
p:ISR: Israel's money is the shekel and its central bank is the Bank of Israel. It scores 25 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. On 29 April 2002 State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg reported that former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned, approved by a senior official who reported to him; Goldberg did not say whether the state should demand the money back. On 3 February 2009 Globes reported that a draft comptroller report alleged flaws in the bank's supervision of Bank Hapoalim's sub-prime investments, on which Hapoalim wrote off 1.5 billion dollars; the bank said it had responses to all the points, and the allegation is unproven. A further comptroller report, on 17 October 2012, found supervision of the bank's reserves dealing deficient as those reserves grew from 28 to 75 billion dollars; the bank said some issues had been corrected during the audit. Frenkel, governor from 1991 to 2000, came from the International Monetary Fund and later chaired Merrill Lynch International; Stanley Fischer, governor from 2005 to 2013, came from the World Bank, the IMF and Citigroup.
p:ESP: Spain uses the euro, so the Bank of Spain follows rates set by the European Central Bank for 21 countries. In 2002 a Madrid court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio that he ran from his office; a wound-up company, NALVI, had been used from at least 1986 to hide Rubio as the investor, and the ruling could be appealed. On 15 September 2017 Spain's National Court, hearing an appeal by two trade unions, decided not to prosecute the former governor over the 2012 failure of the commercial bank Bankia, and that case was dismissed. José Luis Escrivá, governor from 2024, was earlier chief economist at the bank BBVA. Spain scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:PRT: Portugal uses the euro, so the European Central Bank, not the Banco de Portugal, sets interest rates, for all 21 countries on the euro. A 600-page report by a committee the bank itself appointed, with Boston Consulting Group, found failures in its oversight of Banco Espirito Santo going back a decade, and the bank twice refused parliament's request for it. Parliament's own inquiry into Novo Banco's losses approved its final report on 27 July 2021, concluding that the rescue of Banco Espirito Santo and the 4,900 million euro first capitalisation of Novo Banco were a political fraud, and criticising the Banco de Portugal. At the European Central Bank, the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and financiers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it; the bank declined. Portugal scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence.
p:RUS: The Bank of Russia issues the ruble (RUB). It scores 38 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. Its legal independence scores 0.566 of 1 on one index (1 means the bank holds the power). Government pressure is reported in 5 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, all to cut rates or ease. One bribery case is recorded: in October 2005 Moscow prosecutors indicted Alexei Mishin, a chief legal expert at its Moscow directorate, for accepting a $1 million bribe; the verdict was not found. After the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Western countries froze its assets, estimated at around EUR 300 billion worldwide. On 12 December 2025 the EU agreed to freeze EUR 210 billion of them indefinitely. Its swap lines are with China and Kazakhstan. It is a member and part-owner of the Bank for International Settlements.
p:PAK: The State Bank of Pakistan is the country's central bank. It scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case from 2025 is alleged and unproven. In August 2025 Pakistan Observer reported, citing internal memos and cash slips, that senior officials including an executive director issued bulk fresh banknotes directly to private brokers, who resold them at premiums, with each transaction netting officials at least 2 million rupees in kickbacks. It said no probe had been opened. In January 2014 governor Yaseen Anwar resigned; the Finance Ministry spokesman said he cited personal reasons, while unnamed senior officials said it covered differences with Finance Minister Ishaq Dar over inflation and reserves. Two governors came from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund: Ishrat Husain, appointed in December 1999, and Reza Baqir, appointed in May 2019 after leading the IMF's Debt Policy Division. KPMG and BDO audit its accounts.
p:CHL: Chile's central bank is the Central Bank of Chile, which issues the Chilean peso. It scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. Three cases are still open. On 24 July 2012 three staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million pesos in banknotes being processed for destruction, and a fourth was detained the next day; the bank reported it to the police economic crimes unit and began legal action. In March 2022 someone posing as the finance chief of the US firm RVK sent a false invoice for 205,000 dollars from an address one letter off the real one, and the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors in May 2022, said no official appeared to have taken part deliberately, and dismissed its accounting department head on 23 June 2022; he sued in December seeking 267 million pesos. Joaquin Vial joined its council from the bank BBVA in 2012 and Mario Marcel from the World Bank in 2015. KPMG audits its accounts.
p:ZWE: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe issues the ZiG (ZWG), but foreign currency also circulates under a multicurrency system. It scores 34 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 means fully exposed). Two cases carry official findings. At a September 2019 parliamentary Public Accounts Committee hearing, deputy governor Mlambo confirmed the bank issued $663.8 million in Treasury Bills in 2017-2018 to Sakunda Holdings, owned by presidential ally Kudakwashe Tagwirei, on Finance Ministry instruction. From 2003 to 2013, under governor Gideon Gono, the bank ran 'quasi-fiscal' activities and raided private foreign-currency accounts to fund state operations, leaving debts of close to $1.3 billion. Government pressure was reported in 8 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, all to ease policy, 7 in election periods. In 2009 the MDC demanded Gono's replacement; President Mugabe said he would stay.
p:DEU: Germany uses the euro, and its central bank, the Deutsche Bundesbank, follows the interest rates the European Central Bank sets for the 21 countries that use the currency. Bundesbank president Ernst Welteke resigned on 16 April 2004 after criticism for accepting a free New Year stay at Berlin's Hotel Adlon, paid two years earlier by a commercial bank, Dresdner Bank; the Bundesbank supervises commercial banks, and prosecutors and the Bundesbank had opened inquiries. Two further cases concern the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration between 2016 and 2018 over ECB president Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and the ECB declined its January 2018 recommendation that he give it up; and in 2015 a speech on asset purchases was published only the morning after a private London event. Several leaders have since moved into private finance. Axel Weber went from Bundesbank president to chairman of the bank UBS, and Jens Weidmann was elected chairman of Commerzbank's supervisory board on 31 May 2023. Joachim Nagel left the Bundesbank board for the state lender KfW, then the Bank for International Settlements, and has been Bundesbank president since January 2022. Baker Tilly audits the accounts. Germany scores 23 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:LBY: The Central Bank of Libya issues the dinar; Britain's De La Rue prints the notes. The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people over a scheme to seize 128 million US dollars and 5 million euros from the bank's Sirte branch in 2013, sentencing them to 15 and 13 years. In November 2022 the bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar notes, an unproven allegation. Global Witness reported in 2020 and 2021 that governor Saddek Elkaber chairs ABC International Bank in London, which the central bank indirectly owns, calling this a conflict of interest while alleging no lawbreaking. On 18 August 2024 the Presidential Council decreed that governor Sadiq al-Kabir be replaced; a week later the Dbeibah government sent a delegation to take over his office, al-Kabir said he had fled over militia threats, and banking operations were suspended. It scores 49 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.
p:CHE: Switzerland's money is the Swiss franc, and its central bank is the Swiss National Bank, which has shareholders: 100,000 shares, 25 million francs of capital. At the end of 2025, 26 cantons held 38.995%, 24 cantonal banks 11.966% and 19 municipalities 0.265%. Private shareholders held 48.774%, including Theo Siegert at 5.01%. Berne held 6.63% and Zurich 5.23%. The Confederation is not a shareholder, and voting rights of shareholders outside the public sector are capped at 100 shares. It scores 30 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case is recorded. Chairman Philipp Hildebrand resigned on 9 January 2012 after reports that dollar trades in 2011 from a joint account with his wife earned tens of thousands of dollars while the bank was acting to weaken the franc. He said the trades broke no rules but he could not prove he was unaware of them, and he donated the profits to charity. He then joined BlackRock as vice chairman; no ethics finding is recorded for that move.
p:SWE: Sveriges Riksbank is Sweden's central bank and issues the krona. It scores 13 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Two linked cases are recorded from 2020 to 2021. On 18 June 2021 the Riksbank stated that a routine check of staff share dealings found a few employees had made trades not in line with its ethics rules, including trades close to policy decisions and in companies whose bonds it was buying. It called this inappropriate, talked with those involved and began revising the rules. After media reports that Stefan Ingves and Skingsley had conflicts of interest from share holdings when deciding on corporate bond purchases, the bank's General Council reviewed it. On 17 December 2021 it concluded the link was too weak to be a conflict of interest and found no shortcoming in their conduct. Ingves was appointed governor in October 2005 after leading a department at the International Monetary Fund. That move is not an accusation.
p:GHA: The Bank of Ghana issues the cedi. Ghana scores 33 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two cases are documented. In a February 2023 statement the bank said its claims on the government at the end of 2022 included a 37.9 billion cedi overdraft to cover auction shortfalls and maturing bonds, 7.2 billion cedis of treasury bonds bought from banks and 8.9 billion cedis of International Monetary Fund money passed on, although all three had earlier adopted zero deficit financing. In February 2020 the Attorney-General charged former finance minister and governor Kwabena Duffuor and seven others with 68 counts over uniBank's collapse: Duffuor with dishonestly receiving 663.28 million cedis and money laundering, and former second deputy governor Johnson Asiama with approving a 300 million cedi unsecured credit facility from the distressed uniBank to Universal Merchant Bank. Neither accusation reached a verdict. Around 30 January 2025 the Attorney-General withdrew all charges against Asiama, and on 22 July 2025 ended the uniBank case against Duffuor and the others, after recovering more than 60 percent of the funds allegedly lost. Governors have been pushed out before, Henry Kofi Wampah in 2016 and Abdul Nashiru Issahaku in 2017.
p:MOZ: Mozambique's central bank is the Bank of Mozambique. It scores 43 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Four cases concern the 'hidden debts', over 2 billion dollars of loans from Credit Suisse and Russia's VTB. Letters from 2013 had the bank authorising Proindicus to seek 372 million dollars, later 622 million, and Ematum 850 million; board member Silvia de Abreu signed them after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who denied responsibility in 2016. At the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 Gove testified that he signed for reasons of sovereignty and national security and admitted irregularities; judge Efigenio Baptista rejected his reading of the law barring such approvals. In April 2023 Noticias reported Gove and two other board members among four accused in a second trial being prepared; that is unproven. President Filipe Nyusi fired deputy governor Antonio Pinto de Abreu on 26 January 2016 without giving a reason, and replaced Gove that August. On 2 September 2026 President Daniel Chapo revoked Waldemar Fernando de Sousa's appointment as governor and named Felisberto Dinis Navalha; the Attorney General's Office accuses De Sousa over the hidden debts, though he was not tried in the main case.
p:GEO: The National Bank of Georgia issues the lari. It scores 26 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its law scores 0.847 of 1 for independence from government. On 17 July 2015 parliament voted 80 to 19 to move banking supervision to a new agency, after Bidzina Ivanishvili blamed the bank and its chairman Giorgi Kadagidze for the lari's fall. In September 2023 the bank unfroze assets tied to Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General sanctioned by the US Treasury, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a conviction in a Georgian court. Acting president Natia Turnava confirmed on 20 September that she had changed the sanctions procedure single-handedly, after TBC Bank and Bank of Georgia had frozen his accounts; three of the bank's four vice presidents and an adviser resigned. In 2026 the Prosecutor's Office began investigating Council member Nana Keinishvili over possible unlawful involvement in business, after complaints from crypto firm Bitexchange LLC, which the bank had fined; it was still open in October 2026 and nothing is proven.
p:NPL: Nepal Rastra Bank issues the rupee (NPR), held at a fixed rate to India's rupee. It scores 28 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 fully exposed), and 0.652 of 1 for independence in law on Romelli's 42 rules (1 means the bank holds the power, 0 the government). Three cases are recorded. In 2022 the government suspended governor Adhikari over charges of leaking information about government decisions; on 19 April the Supreme Court stayed the suspension and he returned to work. In 2007 a state commission charged governor Bhattarai and executive director Pradhan with embezzlement over hiring American consultants, and the Supreme Court later cleared both. In October 2011 Note Printing Australia pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign officials to win banknote business with Nepal in 2000-2002; the officials are not named.
p:IRN: The Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran issues the rial, which is in free fall. Its law leaves most of the power with government, 0.448 of 1 where 1 means the bank holds it. The government replaced governor Valiollah Seif on 25 July 2018 without reason, then dismissed his successor Abdolnasser Hemmati on 30 May 2021 for standing for president. In October 2021 a Tehran court sentenced Seif to ten years, his deputy Araghchi to eight and the intermediary Salar Aghakhani to thirteen over an illegal foreign-currency scheme; the Supreme Court overturned the verdicts in 2023, and the prosecution of Seif and Araghchi was dropped in March 2025. Abroad, Bahrain's courts convicted the bank of laundering money through Future Bank, fining it one million Bahraini dinars in November 2020 and upholding that in 2021. It scores 43 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, 27th of 194.
p:MWI: The Reserve Bank of Malawi issues the kwacha (MWK). It scores 35 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 fully exposed), and 0.742 of 1 for independence in law on Romelli's 42 rules (1 means the bank holds the power, 0 the government). After a forensic audit of 2019-2020 payments, the state charged four people with abuse of office, negligence, money laundering and causing loss of public funds, alleging K4.3 billion was paid to FDH Bank without board approval; pleas were not taken. In December 2021 police arrested Kabambe and Mwanamvekha and alleged they falsified reserve returns to make the IMF believe Malawi met loan conditions. President Lazarus Chakwera dismissed governor Dalitso Kabambe on 8 July 2020. In 2026-01 President Peter Mutharika appointed Henry Mathanga deputy governor; the bank had dismissed him after a disciplinary inquiry and he faces criminal charges.
p:VNM: The State Bank of Vietnam issues the dong (VND) and holds it in a crawling peg, a slowly adjusted rate against the US dollar. It scores 33 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 fully exposed). Its law scores 0.301 of 1 for independence on Romelli's 42 rules (1 means the bank holds the power, 0 the government), 154th of 155 places, and government pressure was reported in 6 of 37 quarters in 2010-2018. In April 2024 Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced Van Thinh Phat chair Truong My Lan to death for fraud at Saigon Commercial Bank, finding she ordered subordinates to bribe State Bank inspectors; state media said head inspector Do Thi Nhan received $5.2 million. In October 2011 Securency pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to Vietnamese officials to win banknote business in 2001-2004.
p:IRQ: The Central Bank of Iraq issues the dinar (IQD), held within a band of 2% or less against the US dollar. It scores 36 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 fully exposed), and 0.733 of 1 for independence in law on Romelli's 42 rules (1 means the bank holds the power, 0 the government). In 2012 Iraq's Board of Supreme Audit found that most transactions in the bank's daily dollar auctions rested on fraudulent paperwork, and its top auditor told US officials that up to $800 million a week was leaving Iraq illegally. In October 2012 the cabinet removed governor Sinan al-Shabibi after a parliamentary committee charged that bank officials were abusing the dollar sales. The Supreme Judicial Council confirmed arrest warrants for him and other officials without giving the charges. His defence called the case politically motivated. No court outcome was found.
p:KOR: South Korea's money is the won, issued by the Bank of Korea, which scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Two cases are recorded, both ending in conviction. Between 2022 and 2023 a currency-exchange employee at the bank's Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the rule that older coins leave the vault first, at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 one-hundred-won coins from 2018 and 2019 go out ahead of 2017 coins; the collector made about 180 million won selling them and gave the employee about 55 million, and the Daejeon District Court imposed two years and six months in prison, a fine and confiscation of about 43.31 million won. Between 2013 and 2015 an employee handling receipts from the bank's publication sales diverted about 56 million won to a personal account and spent about 12 million won on commemorative banknote sheets with a company card; the Seoul Central District Court convicted the employee and gave eight months suspended for two years, the money having been repaid. Two officials came from international lenders: Hwang Geon-il of the World Bank was nominated to the rate-setting Monetary Policy Committee, and Rhee Chang-yong of the International Monetary Fund was nominated governor on 23 March 2022.
p:VEN: The Central Bank of Venezuela issues the bolivar (VES, VED). It scores 37 of 100 on exposure to outside influence (0 means shielded, 100 fully exposed), and 0.816 of 1 for independence in law on Romelli's 42 rules (1 means the bank holds the power, 0 the government). Government pressure was reported in 18 of 37 quarters in 2010-2018, including 13 demands to print money. In 2017-01 President Nicolas Maduro announced the firing of bank chief Nelson Merentes. In January 2020 prosecutor Tarek William Saab said a payments head and others forged procurement files so the bank paid about $1.7 million to three companies it had not contracted, for goods never delivered; eight arrest warrants were requested, and these are the prosecutor's allegations. On 29 July 2022 London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the Maduro-appointed board should be disregarded, keeping more than $1bn of gold at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
p:BOL: The Central Bank of Bolivia issues the country's money. Bolivia scores 30 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and its weakest side is the corruption and secrecy around the bank, at 69. On 17 December 2019 Guillermo Aponte became interim president, replacing Pablo Ramos, who was under investigation over alleged favouring of illicit enrichment; that remains unproven. On 28 April 2026 La Paz prosecutors had former president Edwin Rojas and three other former senior officials detained over seven debt-swap operations in June and July 2024, in which the bank dealt with local financial entities at inflated prices, costing the state 142.3 million US dollars. The transparency vice ministry said price records were later altered on internal email instructions. Seven people are under investigation, the suspects deny wrongdoing, Rojas invoked his right to silence, and no formal charge has been brought.
p:SMR: San Marino uses the euro, and its central bank is the Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino. It scores 45 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, mainly because its money is issued or backed from abroad. The bank is owned mostly by the state: the Eccellentissima Camera della Repubblica di San Marino holds 72%, four banks hold the rest: Cassa di Risparmio della Repubblica di San Marino 16%, Banca di San Marino 6%, Banca Agricola Commerciale Istituto Bancario Sammarinese 5% and Banca Sammarinese di Investimento 1%, as of 31 December 2025. One case is recorded, from 2019 to 2020, over a 220,000 euro payment from the bank to Sandro Gozi for a consultancy that investigators suspected was fictitious. The case, against Gozi and bank president Catia Tomasetti, became public in April 2019. The Tribunal of San Marino dismissed it in 2020, finding no relevant conduct by either suspect; the article reports the consultancy was real.
p:UKR: The National Bank of Ukraine issues the hryvnia. Ukraine scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around the bank, at 59. Its independence written into law is high, 0.893 of 1 and rank 22 of 155, but its governors have been pushed. In January 2009 parliament voted no confidence in governor Volodymyr Stelmakh, 227 of 450 seats in favour, as the hryvnia lost nearly half its value; President Viktor Yushchenko's office called the vote illegal and kept backing him. In July 2020 governor Yakiv Smolii resigned, telling President Volodymyr Zelensky that systematic political pressure had been exerted on the bank. One case is open: on 11 November 2019 the National Anti-Corruption Bureau detained seven people, including former first deputy governor Pysaruk, on suspicion of embezzling 1.2 billion hryvnia from a 2014 stabilisation loan the bank made to VAB Bank; it is unproven.
p:PRY: The Central Bank of Paraguay issues the country's currency. It scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. In January 2003 impeachment proceedings began against President Luis Gonzalez Macchi over an alleged 26 million dollar embezzlement from the bank, and the Senate vote fell short in February. On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion gave him six years for breach of trust over the diversion of 16 million dollars from two private banks the central bank had taken over, Union and Orienta, and gave its former banking superintendent Jose Pecci eight years; an appeals court later cleared him for insufficient evidence. President Nicanor Duarte Frutos dismissed bank president Monica Perez in February 2007 over disagreements with the government's economic team. On 13 July 2021 an anti-money-laundering police unit searched the bank over embezzlement and money laundering, after its supervision authority refused prosecutors documents on bank secrecy grounds. On 3 November 2026 governor Carlos Carvallo resigned at President Santiago Pena's request, after a prosecutor sought a criminal investigation around the digital lender ueno and arrest orders went out for eight people linked to it; Carvallo had headed ueno until August 2023, and Pena was a partner in its owner until March 2025.
p:NOR: Norges Bank issues the Norwegian krone and is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. It is among the least exposed to outside influence on this map, 18 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed. Its one recorded trouble is the 2020 hiring of Nicolai Tangen to run the country's oil fund. The bank's Supervisory Council warned that the appointment risked breaking laws, rules and guidelines, saying Tangen still appeared to be the main owner of the investment firm AKO Capital with voting control although the bank said he had cut those ties. After the Storting's finance committee raised the same concern, the Executive Board revised his terms in August 2020: he would give up his holding in AKO Capital LLP and hand it and its dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said guidelines, regulations and laws had been breached. EY audits the bank from 2022 to 2027, and at the end of 2025 103 outside firms ran mandates worth 1,062 billion kroner for it. A United States line of up to 30 billion US dollars, agreed on 19 March 2020, expired on 31 December 2021.
p:CHN: The People's Bank of China issues the renminbi. It scores 34 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 65. Written independence from government scores 0.659 of 1 on an index of 42 legal rules, but the part covering the governor and the board scores 0.04. Government pressure was reported in 2 of 37 quarters surveyed from 2010 to 2018. One case is documented: in October 2024 the Huanggang Intermediate People's Court sentenced former deputy governor Fan Yifei to death with a two-year reprieve, to be commuted to life without parole, for accepting property worth more than 386 million yuan through his posts at the bank and elsewhere, including China Construction Bank. Its reach is wide: 89 swap lines, agreements to lend its currency to another central bank, 8.6 percent of world currency trading and 2,346.4 tonnes of gold.
p:AZE: The Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan issues the currency coded AZN, which is held at a de facto peg to the US dollar (a fixed rate). It scores 31 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it (62). Its written independence from government scores 0.732 of 1 on Romelli's 42 rules. In April 2022 parliament approved President Ilham Aliyev's proposal to replace governor Elman Rustamov, in post since 1995, with Pasha Bank chief Taleh Kazimov; no reason was reported. Two cases are documented. A Vienna court found that banknote printer OeBS overcharged the bank by 20% and that the kickback returned to local decision makers; OeBS managers were convicted in 2014 and on retrial in 2018, and no Azerbaijani official was named. In September 2009 a Baku court sentenced six former officers to terms from a two-year suspended sentence to eight years for embezzling AZN 1.4 million.
p:THA: The Bank of Thailand issues the baht and is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. Its law leaves much of the power with government, 0.435 of 1 where 1 means the bank holds it. On 29 May 2001 the government fired governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul after Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said he was not satisfied with the bank's low interest rates. Finance Minister Kittiratt Na-Ranong later pressed for governor Prasarn Trairatvorakul's replacement over the 2.75 percent rate, and in May 2024 Pheu Thai leader Paetongtarn Shinawatra said the bank's independence obstructs fixing the economy. A 2001 case against former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, over using reserves to defend the baht in the Asian financial crisis, ended in 2016 with the Supreme Court upholding that he had not acted improperly. Former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee was convicted of malfeasance for putting representatives of supervised banks on the committee that picks the bank's board.
p:SUR: The Central Bank of Suriname issues the currency coded SRD. It scores 30 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it (63). Its written independence from government scores 0.514 of 1 on the Cukierman method, rank 126 of 191. Two cases ended in convictions. On 31 January 2022 a court convicted former governor van Trikt of violating the Anti-Corruption Act, forgery, embezzlement, money laundering and taking part in a criminal enterprise, in a case involving over $800,000, and sentenced him to eight years and a S$500,000 fine; the bank's legal director and others were also convicted. In December 2021 a court sentenced Hoefdraad in absentia to 12 years for conspiring to defraud the bank while he was finance minister; on appeal on 19 January 2026 the court imposed 10 years and dropped the criminal-organisation count. It has three swap lines with China, and it is not known whether they are in force.
p:LBR: The Central Bank of Liberia issues the currency coded LRD. It scores 30 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it (68). Its written independence from government scores 0.715 of 1 on Romelli's 42 rules. In July 2024 Liberia suspended governor Tarlue indefinitely after an audit report on 2018-2023 found irregularities in the bank's lending to the government, including more than $80 million in apparently unauthorised financing for salary payments. In March 2019 a Monrovia court ordered former deputy governor Sirleaf, former governor Weeks and official Hagba held for trial on charges including theft and criminal conspiracy, over banknotes printed in 2016-2018 that could not be accounted for. Liberia's Presidential Investigation Team alleged that printer Crane Currency conspired with bank officials to print L$18,151,000,000 beyond the contracted L$15 billion; Crane denied wrongdoing and kickbacks.
p:COL: The Bank of the Republic issues Colombia's peso (COP) and is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. It scores 26 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed. Its written independence from government scores 0.757 of 1 on Romelli's 42 rules, rank 62 of 155, and the law was last changed in 1992. Government pressure was reported in 2 of 37 quarters in 2010-2018, each time to cut rates. On 31 July 2025 President Gustavo Petro accused the bank of wanting to "finish off the economy" and of having an electoral bet, after its board voted 4-3 to hold the rate at 9.25%. In 2011 two bank officials, investigated for allegedly giving reserved information to the DAS security agency, had a one-month suspension revoked on appeal by the Procuraduría, which found they broke no rule.
p:MNE: The Central Bank of Montenegro does not issue money. Montenegro uses the euro, which it adopted unilaterally: the Deutsche Mark became sole legal tender on 1 January 2001 and the euro replaced it in March 2002. The bank does not issue euros, is not a member of the European System of Central Banks and has a repo line (a short-term loan arrangement) of up to EUR 250 million with the Eurosystem. It scores 33 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed. Its written independence from government scores 0.79 of 1 on Romelli's 42 rules. Three cases are documented, all alleged and unproven. In 2018 the bank's Council reportedly found that deputy governor Irena Radović put personal interest first and disclosed business secrets; she called this retaliation. The NGO MANS said five payments totaling €4,100 went to relatives of governor Radoje Žugić in 2017-2018; he reportedly said he did not act illegally. In 2012 MANS alleged that First Bank received a €44 million state loan in 2008 that it could not repay.
p:COD: The Central Bank of the Congo issues the country's money. It scores 33 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In April 2021 Congo's state finance inspectorate found that 43 million US dollars moved from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to the food importer Egal was an embezzlement of public funds, and that the bank kept false accounts to cover it: its 2013 books showed about 43.1 million dollars in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 dollars. On 25 October 2023 the accounts of former governor Deogratias Mutombo, and of Albert Yuma, once board chairman of the mining company Gecamines, were frozen over an alleged embezzlement of 25.521 million dollars. Belgium's federal prosecutor also opened a money laundering investigation into Mutombo and five others, with searches in September 2023; as of October 2024 no suspect had been charged.
p:NZL: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand issues the New Zealand dollar. It scores 23 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed, less exposed than 91% of the 194 places scored, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. On 10 March 2016 the decision on the Official Cash Rate, the interest rate the bank sets, leaked from its media lock-up before release. Deloitte, engaged on 11 March 2016 and reporting on 12 April 2016, traced it to a Mediaworks employee: one journalist emailed a draft story out of the lock-up, and another emailed the economics blogger Michael Reddell at 8.04am, before the 9am announcement. Mediaworks reported itself on 5 April 2016, and the bank ended embargoed lock-ups. It part-owns the Bank for International Settlements, and Note Printing Australia prints its banknotes.
p:AFG: Da Afghanistan Bank is Afghanistan's central bank and issues the afghani. It scores 33 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption in the country. A May 2011 report by the High Office of Oversight and Anticorruption said the bank monitored Kabul Bank poorly; Kabul Bank had $925 million in outstanding loans, many undocumented, before the central bank took it over in 2010. After the Taliban takeover, the US froze nearly $9.5 billion of the bank's assets on 17 August 2021, much of it held at the New York Federal Reserve. On 11 February 2022 President Biden signed an order to split $7 billion of the frozen funds: $3.5 billion for Afghan relief and $3.5 billion kept in the US for litigation by US victims of terrorism.
p:UGA: The Bank of Uganda is the central bank that issues the Ugandan shilling. It scores 32 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption in the country and money-laundering risk in its banks. One case is recorded. A confidential 2018 Auditor General report to parliament said bank managers, including governor Mutebile, acted without guidelines, regulations or policies and may have intentionally neglected aspects of the closure and sale of at least seven commercial banks, including Crane Bank in 2016-2017. These are findings of a report, not court verdicts. Sudhir Ruparelia, dfcu Bank and Nile River Acquisition Company are named in the case. Uganda has had 1 systemic banking crisis since 1970.
p:MDV: The Maldives Monetary Authority issues the Maldivian rufiyaa and scores 36 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Its record turns on one scandal, the embezzlement of 1.3 billion rufiyaa from the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. In February 2019 the Anti-Corruption Commission found the authority negligent: its Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a 59 million US dollar cheque from that company to a firm called SOF but did not examine SOF's large transactions through the Bank of Maldives and the Bank of Ceylon. Its former head, Ibrahim Athif Shakoor, said governor Azeema Adam objected to filing a police report. In March 2019 police confirmed they were investigating governor Ahmed Naseer for obstruction of justice, and he resigned that July amid claims he had got around the bank's rules and interfered in the unit's inquiries, one into a 22.5 million rufiyaa deposit to then-president Abdulla Yameen's account before the 2018 election; Naseer denied it. Prosecutors charged Shakoor in February 2020 with money laundering for failing to report the irregularities, and on 14 October 2025 withdrew the charge, with no conviction. India agreed a currency-borrowing line with the authority on 7 October 2024.
p:SGP: The Monetary Authority of Singapore is the central bank that issues the Singapore dollar. It scores 22 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed, making it less exposed than 93% of 194 places scored; its weakest side is that the country's laws hide who owns money. No documented case was found. Under a 1967 agreement, Brunei and Singapore accept each other's notes and coins at par. The bank is part-owner of the Bank for International Settlements, which 63 central banks own, and belongs to the Financial Stability Board. Former chairman Tharman Shanmugaratnam is a member of the Group of Thirty. It has 16 swap lines (agreements to borrow another central bank's currency). Note Printing Australia prints its banknotes.
p:SRB: The National Bank of Serbia issues the Serbian dinar. It scores 27 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 61. A bill expected to pass on 15 July would have placed the bank under government control and allowed the dismissal of governor Mladjan Dinkic. Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic wanted a devaluation Dinkic resisted, and members of the DOS coalition said a party official cannot be governor; Dinkic said the law would make the bank dependent on government and parliament, and the authorities said that had no foundation. On 18 July 2003 he resigned, with two of the bank's three deputy governors, after parliament passed a law he said undermined the bank's independence by letting members of parliament appoint its top officials. On 11 January 2006 police arrested vice-governor Dejan Simić on suspicion of taking bribes; an investigation was ordered and the bank's Council removed him on 16 January 2006. No indictment or verdict has followed.
p:MNG: The Bank of Mongolia issues the tugrik. Two cases and two departures centre on N. Zoljargal, governor from 2012, who was replaced on 20 July 2016, two years before his term was due to end and with no reason given. The anti-corruption agency IAAC arrested him on 29 November 2017 over the Chinggis bond and a price-stabilising programme; a court released him with a travel ban and prosecutors had not charged him. In April 2020 he and three politicians were reported charged with abuse of power over transferring 49 percent of the Erdenet Mining Company; those charges are unproven. Lawmakers accepted the resignation of his successor, Nadmid Bayartsaikhan, on 21 November 2019, after the Financial Action Task Force put Mongolia on its grey list over money-laundering enforcement. The bank holds two currency swap lines with China and scores 31 of 100 for exposure to outside influence.
p:ECU: Ecuador uses the US dollar as its only legal tender, adopted in January 2000 at 25,000 sucres per dollar, so its Central Bank of Ecuador does not issue its own money. The bank scores 31 of 100 for outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is corruption in the country and money-laundering risk in its banks.
