n:High Court of England and Wales: The High Court of England and Wales is a court in London. It is named in an event involving the Central Bank of Venezuela. On 29 July 2022 it ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the central bank board appointed by Maduro should be disregarded. The ruling kept more than 1 billion dollars of Venezuelan gold held at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
n:Bank of England: The Bank of England is the central bank of the United Kingdom, based in London. It holds more than 1 billion dollars of Venezuelan gold belonging to the Central Bank of Venezuela. On 29 July 2022 London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the central bank board appointed by Maduro should be disregarded. The gold stayed out of Maduro's control.
n:Venezuelan Supreme Court: The Venezuelan Supreme Court is the country's highest court, in Caracas. It is named in an event involving the Central Bank of Venezuela. Its judgments backed the central bank board appointed by Maduro. On 29 July 2022 London's High Court ruled that those judgments should be disregarded, which kept more than 1 billion dollars of Venezuelan gold at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
n:Juan Guaidó: Juan Guaidó is a Venezuelan opposition figure whose appointees claimed to run the Central Bank of Venezuela, the institution that issues the country's money. He is named in a court case over the bank's gold. On 29 July 2022 London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the board appointed by President Nicolás Maduro should be disregarded. The ruling kept more than 1 billion dollars of Venezuelan gold held at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
n:Guaidó-appointed BCV board: This is the board of the Central Bank of Venezuela (BCV, the institution that issues the country's money) that was appointed by opposition figure Juan Guaidó, in competition with the board appointed by President Nicolás Maduro. It is named in a court case over the bank's gold. On 29 July 2022 London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the Maduro-appointed board should be disregarded. The ruling kept more than 1 billion dollars of Venezuelan gold at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
n:Nicolás Maduro: Nicolás Maduro is president of Venezuela and is based in Caracas. He is tied to the Central Bank of Venezuela, which issues the country's money. He announced the firing of the bank's chief, Nelson Merentes, who the report says handed in his resignation, and named economist Ricardo Sanguino to succeed him. The report gives no reason from Maduro and no statement from Merentes, and places the firing amid an economic crisis and a badly handled release of larger banknotes. Maduro is also named in a case in which London's High Court ruled on 29 July 2022 that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing his appointed bank board should be disregarded, keeping more than 1 billion dollars of gold at the Bank of England out of his control.
n:Polish ruling-coalition MPs: These are members of parliament from Poland's governing coalition, based in Warsaw. They filed a motion on 26 March 2024 to bring Adam Glapiński, president of the National Bank of Poland (the central bank), before the State Tribunal, a court that can try senior officials. The motion lists eight charges, including bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and currency interventions carried out without authorization. These are accusations, and no outcome is recorded for this motion.
n:State Tribunal (Poland): The State Tribunal is a court in Warsaw. It is tied to the National Bank of Poland through a motion that members of parliament from the governing coalition filed on 26 March 2024 to bring the bank's president, Adam Glapiński, before it. The motion lists eight charges, including bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and currency interventions carried out without authorization. These are accusations, and no ruling by the Tribunal is recorded.
n:Sejm Committee for Constitutional Resp: This is a committee of the Sejm, Poland's lower house of parliament, in Warsaw. It handles the case against Adam Glapiński, president of the National Bank of Poland. It backed a 148-page report upholding all eight charges against him, including 144 billion zloty of bond purchases in 2020 and 2021. A full Sejm vote must wait at least 21 days, and an indictment could suspend him. The charges are accusations that have not been decided by a court. The report was dated 12 October 2026.
n:Government of Hungary: The Government of Hungary, based in Budapest, is tied to Magyar Nemzeti Bank, the country's central bank. On 12 March 2024 the bank said a proposed law widening its supervisory board's control over activities outside its basic tasks could erode its independence, amid pressure on Governor György Matolcsy to cut interest rates. On 14 May 2025 the government proposed changes that would ban the bank from creating new foundations, add a fourth deputy governor and enlarge its monetary policy committee from nine to 11 members. An earlier report describes a bill cutting governor András Simor's monthly pay by 75 percent, from about 8 million to 2 million forints, through a cap on everyone paid from public funds. A government spokesman said this did not threaten the bank's independence; the European Central Bank said such changes should apply only to future appointments.
n:Javier Milei: Javier Milei is president of Argentina and is based in Buenos Aires. He is tied to the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic. On 30 July 2026 he announced a bill to change the bank's charter. It would restore a single goal of preserving the currency's value, bar the bank from issuing money to finance the state or buying government bonds when they are first sold, and limit its profit transfers to the Treasury to debt repayment. No outcome for the bill is recorded.
n:Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is president of Brazil and is based in Brasília. He is tied to the Central Bank of Brazil. On 21 June 2024 he called the bank's president, Roberto Campos Neto, his political and ideological adversary and said that when he could replace him at year-end, Brazil would return to normality. This is a public statement of pressure, and no further outcome is recorded.
n:Gustavo Petro: Gustavo Petro is president of Colombia and is based in Bogotá. He is tied to the Bank of the Republic, Colombia's central bank. On 31 July 2025, after the bank's board voted 4 to 3 to keep its interest rate at 9.25 percent, he accused it of wanting to finish off the economy and of having an electoral bet. No further outcome is recorded.
n:Jean-Pierre Oyiba: Jean-Pierre Oyiba was chief of staff to Gabon's president. He is tied to the Bank of Central African States (BEAC), the central bank shared by several countries in the region. A November 2009 internal BEAC report found about 20 billion CFA francs had been diverted from the bank's Paris office to 139 beneficiaries between 2004 and 2008. It said Oyiba received about 100,000 euros. He resigned on 9 November 2009 after the report came out, and he denies receiving the money. On 28 September 2012 a court in Mfoundi, Cameroon, sentenced another person, Kemadjou, to life in prison and ordered him to pay BEAC 26.4 billion CFA francs.
n:Pisa de Guatemala: Pisa de Guatemala is a drug company based in Guatemala. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of Guatemala, the central bank. In May 2015 the bank's president, Julio Suárez, was arrested along with other board members of the social security institute (IGSS). Prosecutors said they took part in the irregular award of a 116 million quetzal contract (about 14.5 million dollars) to Pisa de Guatemala. The charges were unlawful association, influence peddling, illegal commissions and active bribery. Suárez was later acquitted: the Supreme Court's Criminal Chamber upheld the June 2019 appeal-court acquittal, as reported in October 2021.
n:Ministerio Público de Guatemala: The Ministerio Público is Guatemala's prosecution agency, based in Guatemala City. It is tied to the Bank of Guatemala, the central bank, through a case in which prosecutors investigated the bank's president, Julio Suárez. He was arrested in May 2015 with other board members of the social security institute (IGSS). Prosecutors said they took part in the irregular award of a 116 million quetzal contract (about 14.5 million dollars) to the drug company Pisa de Guatemala. The charges were unlawful association, influence peddling, illegal commissions and active bribery. Suárez was later acquitted: the Supreme Court's Criminal Chamber upheld the June 2019 appeal-court acquittal, as reported in October 2021.
n:CICIG: CICIG is an international body based in Guatemala City. It is tied to the Bank of Guatemala, the central bank, through a case it investigated. n:Corporación Líder Plus 080: Corporación Líder Plus 080 is a company in Venezuela named in a case involving the Central Bank of Venezuela, the institution that issues the country's money. In January 2020 prosecutor Tarek William Saab said a head of payments at the bank and others forged procurement files, so the bank paid about 1.7 million dollars in seven payments to three companies it had not contracted, for overpriced goods that were never delivered. Eight arrest warrants were requested on charges of illegal profit in public administration, diversion of public funds, criminal association and money laundering. The case began with a complaint by the bank's president, Calixto Ortega. These are allegations, and no trial or conviction is reported.

n:Policía de Investigaciones de Chile: The Policía de Investigaciones is Chile's investigative police, based in Santiago. It is tied to the Central Bank of Chile through a case. On 24 July 2012 three bank staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million Chilean pesos in banknotes that were being processed for destruction, and a fourth was detained the next day. The bank itself reported the case, passed it to the police economic crimes unit and began legal action. These are allegations, and no outcome is given.
n:Paraguayan prosecution service: This is the prosecution service of Paraguay, based in Asunción. It is investigating the Central Bank of Paraguay. On 13 July a special anti-money-laundering police unit searched the bank, after the bank's supervision authority declined to give prosecutors documents, citing bank secrecy laws. The investigation concerns embezzlement and money laundering and is linked to the Fifa-gate investigations, the corruption cases around world football's governing body. No individuals are named and no charges are reported.
n:Senate of Paraguay: The Senate of Paraguay sits in Asunción. It is tied to the Central Bank of Paraguay through impeachment proceedings against President Luis González Macchi, which began in January 2003. He was accused, among other things, of embezzling 26 million dollars from the central bank. Later reports describe 16 million dollars taken from two bankrupt private banks that the state had taken over. In February 2003 the Senate vote fell short, with 25 of 44 votes where 30 were needed. A court sentenced him to six years in June 2006, and an appeals court later cleared him, saying the evidence was insufficient.
n:Chamber of Deputies of Paraguay: The Chamber of Deputies is the lower house of Paraguay's parliament, based in Asunción. n:Corte Nacional de Justicia del Ecuador: This is Ecuador's National Court of Justice, based in Quito. It is tied to the Central Bank of Ecuador through the case of the bank's former president, Pedro Delgado. On 8 January 2019 the court sentenced him to five years in prison, repayment of 788,855.94 dollars, forfeiture of assets and public apologies. The prosecutor's office described the crime as unlawful association, while the court's own post called it illicit enrichment. The same source reports a 2015 embezzlement conviction carrying eight years, and says he allegedly allowed large loans without proper documents or guarantees while leading the bank.
n:Fiscalía General del Estado (Ecuador): The Fiscalía General del Estado is Ecuador's prosecutor's office, based in Quito. It is tied to the Central Bank of Ecuador through the case of the bank's former president, Pedro Delgado. On 8 January 2019 Ecuador's National Court of Justice sentenced him to five years in prison, repayment of 788,855.94 dollars, forfeiture of assets and public apologies. n:Contraloría General de la República de: This is Nicaragua's Comptroller General, the state auditor, based in Managua. In 2007 it concluded that the board of the Central Bank of Nicaragua sold certificates called CENI, issued to cover the collapse of banks, for less than market value, and then raised interest rates to benefit the main buyer, Bancentro. The fraud is described as 500 million dollars. The Comptroller alleged criminal involvement by six men, including former finance minister Eduardo Montealegre, who denied wrongdoing and called it a political witch hunt. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including Montealegre. The report names no central bank officials among them and gives no court ruling. It says former central bank president Francisco Mayorga was already found guilty in the banking scandal.
n:Bancentro: Bancentro is a bank based in Managua, Nicaragua. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including Montealegre. The report gives no court ruling for them, and says former central bank president Francisco Mayorga was already found guilty in the banking scandal.
n:Eduardo Montealegre: Eduardo Montealegre is a former finance minister of Nicaragua. He is named in a case involving the Central Bank of Nicaragua. In 2007 the Comptroller General concluded that the central bank board sold certificates called CENI, issued to cover the collapse of banks, for less than market value, and then raised interest rates to benefit the main buyer, Bancentro. The fraud is described as 500 million dollars. The Comptroller alleged criminal involvement by six men, including Montealegre, who denied wrongdoing and called it a political witch hunt. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including him. The report gives no court ruling on those charges. These are allegations.
n:Armando Juárez: Armando Juárez is a person in Nicaragua who is tied to the Central Bank of Nicaragua through an audit and investigation case. In 2007 the country's Comptroller General concluded that the central bank board sold certificates called CENI, issued to cover the collapse of banks, for less than market value, and then raised interest rates to benefit the main buyer, Bancentro. The fraud is described as 500 million dollars. The Comptroller alleged criminal involvement by six men, including former finance minister Eduardo Montealegre, who denied wrongdoing. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including Montealegre, and the report gives no court ruling on them.
n:Bank of Credit and Commerce Internatio: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) was a bank based in London. A 1991 New York grand-jury indictment alleged it paid 3 million dollars in bribes in return for depositing part of the 1986 and 1987 reserves of the Central Reserve Bank of Peru, the country's central bank, in BCCI's Panama branch. The Peruvian bank's board approved moving 100 million dollars and later doubling it. The indictment did not name central bank officials. The Christian Science Monitor identified Figueroa and Neyra in the matter, and both strenuously denied the charges; Neyra called the decision purely technical. All Peruvian deposits were withdrawn by the end of 1987.
n:New York State grand jury: This is a New York State grand jury, a group of citizens that decides whether to bring criminal charges. In 1991 it indicted the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), alleging 3 million dollars in bribes in return for depositing part of Peru's 1986 and 1987 reserves, held by the Central Reserve Bank of Peru, in BCCI's Panama branch. The central bank's board approved moving 100 million dollars and later doubling it. The indictment did not name central bank officials. The Christian Science Monitor identified Figueroa and Neyra in the matter, and both strenuously denied the charges. All Peruvian deposits were withdrawn by the end of 1987.
n:Peruvian parliamentary commission: This is a commission of Peru's parliament, based in Lima. It is tied to the Central Reserve Bank of Peru, the country's central bank, through the bribery matter around the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI). A 1991 New York grand-jury indictment of BCCI alleged 3 million dollars in bribes in return for depositing part of Peru's 1986 and 1987 reserves in BCCI's Panama branch. The central bank's board approved moving 100 million dollars and later doubling it. The indictment did not name central bank officials. The Christian Science Monitor identified Figueroa and Neyra, and both strenuously denied the charges. All Peruvian deposits were withdrawn by the end of 1987.
n:Procuraduría General de la Nación: The Procuraduría General de la Nación is Colombia's public oversight agency, based in Bogotá. It investigated two officials of the Bank of the Republic, Colombia's central bank, who were accused of giving reserved information about people and companies to officials of the DAS security agency. They received a one-month suspension. In January 2011 the bank reported that the Procuraduría's second-instance ruling revoked the suspension, recognizing that the two had broken no rule.
n:Departamento Administrativo de Segurid: The Departamento Administrativo de Seguridad (DAS) was a security agency of Colombia, based in Bogotá. Two officials of the Bank of the Republic, Colombia's central bank, were investigated for allegedly giving reserved information about people and companies to DAS officials, and they received a one-month suspension. In January 2011 the bank reported that the Procuraduría's second-instance ruling revoked the suspension, recognizing that the two had broken no rule.
n:Official Stanford Investors Committee: The Official Stanford Investors Committee is a group based in Dallas that represents victims and creditors of Stanford's collapsed financial business. After the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB), which issues money for several island states, seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua, the committee sued the central bank in Dallas in 2013. It alleged the bank fraudulently misappropriated assets belonging to those victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the ECCB and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law. The court did not rule on whether the allegations were true.
n:US District Court for the Northern Dis: This is a US federal court in Dallas. It heard a suit by the Official Stanford Investors Committee against the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB), which issues money for several island states. After the ECCB seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua, the committee sued in 2013, alleging fraudulent misappropriation of assets belonging to Stanford's victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the ECCB and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law. The court did not rule on whether the allegations were true.
n:Bank of Antigua: The Bank of Antigua is a bank based in Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda, which was owned by Stanford. The Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB), which issues money for several island states, seized it. In 2013 the Official Stanford Investors Committee sued the ECCB in Dallas, alleging it fraudulently misappropriated assets belonging to Stanford's victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the ECCB and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law. The court did not rule on whether the allegations were true.
n:Focus Maritime Corporation: Focus Maritime Corporation is a company, with no stated location, named in a case tied to the Central Bank of Cyprus. A transfer of 1 million euros from the company in 2007, a few months after Christodoulou's term as governor expired, was not declared in accounts from 2007 to 2009. In 2014 he pleaded guilty to six tax offences and was given five months in prison. He had said he had not been bribed.
n:European Central Bank: The European Central Bank, based in Frankfurt, issues the euro and oversees banking in the euro area. It is named in a case tied to the Central Bank of Malta. Governor Scicluna, a former finance minister, pleaded not guilty on 29 May 2024 to fraud and other financial crimes over the government's handling of a private hospital contract, the Vitals concession, while he was finance minister. He stepped aside as governor in July 2024 and was reinstated in July 2025 after the European Central Bank was consulted and raised no objections. The charges are unproven.
n:Bankia: Bankia is a commercial bank based in Madrid that failed in summer 2012. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of Spain, the central bank. On 15 September 2017 Spain's National Court decided by majority, on an appeal filed by two trade unions, not to prosecute the former governor over the failure. The decision was described as final.
n:Audiencia Nacional: The Audiencia Nacional is Spain's National Court, based in Madrid. It is tied to the Bank of Spain, the central bank, through the failure of the commercial bank Bankia in summer 2012. On 15 September 2017 the court decided by majority, on an appeal filed by two trade unions, not to prosecute the bank's former governor. The decision was described as final.
n:NALVI: NALVI is a company in Madrid, already wound up when the case was reported. It is tied to the Bank of Spain, the central bank. In 2002 a Madrid court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio, which De la Concha ran from his office. The report says NALVI was used from at least 1986 to hide Rubio as the investor. The ruling could be appealed.
n:Audiencia Provincial de Madrid: The Audiencia Provincial de Madrid is a court in Madrid. It is tied to the Bank of Spain, the central bank, through a case from 2002. The court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio, which De la Concha ran from his office. The report says a company, NALVI, which had already been wound up, was used from at least 1986 to hide Rubio as the investor. The ruling could be appealed.
n:North Estonian Bank: The North Estonian Bank is a bank based in Tallinn. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of Estonia (Eesti Pank), the central bank, over the loss of 10 million dollars from the North Estonian Bank. A charge of preparing to embezzle was dropped about two weeks before the verdict. On 5 March 1999 the Tallinn City Court found Kallas and Kaju not guilty of abuse of power and of submitting false information.
n:Tallinn City Court: The Tallinn City Court sits in Tallinn, Estonia. It heard a case tied to the Bank of Estonia (Eesti Pank), the central bank, over the loss of 10 million dollars from the North Estonian Bank. A charge of preparing to embezzle had been dropped about two weeks earlier. On 5 March 1999 the court found Kallas and Kaju not guilty of abuse of power and of submitting false information.
n:Crédit Lyonnais: Crédit Lyonnais is a state-owned bank based in Paris. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of France, the central bank. Jean-Claude Trichet was charged with spreading false information and publishing inexact accounts of the bank for 1991 to mid-1993, and prosecutors recommended a 10-month suspended sentence. In June 2003 judges cleared him, writing that he had only imprecise or incorrect information on the losses. Prosecutors had about 10 days to appeal. Jacques de Larosière, Banque de France governor at the time, was also accused; no verdict for him is recorded.
n:Anglo Irish Bank: Anglo Irish Bank is a bank based in Dublin. It is named in a case tied to the Central Bank of Ireland. The matter was 87 million euros in secret directors' loans at Anglo Irish Bank, discovered in January 2008. An internal committee found it was not pursued by the regulator, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing. Neary, the financial regulator, said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008, and said he would retire early over the regulator's handling of it.
n:Irish Nationwide Building Society: The Irish Nationwide Building Society is a financial institution based in Dublin. It is named in a case tied to the Central Bank of Ireland, which concerned the regulator's handling of 87 million euros in secret directors' loans at a different bank, Anglo Irish Bank. An internal committee found the matter, discovered in January 2008, was not pursued, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing. Neary, the financial regulator, said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008, and said he would retire early.
n:Snoras: Snoras was a bank in Vilnius that went bankrupt. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of Lithuania, the central bank. A central bank official who monitored Snoras was sacked in November 2011 and charged with letting Snoras conceal information from the central bank's leadership, including on assets in Swiss banks. A guilty verdict from March 2014 was annulled by a Vilnius court, which found no crime. That ruling can be appealed to the Supreme Court.
n:Commissie Scheltema: The Scheltema committee was set up by Dutch finance minister Wouter Bos and based in The Hague to examine the collapse of DSB bank. In June 2010 it reported that De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch central bank, fell seriously short as DSB's supervisor. It said the central bank missed flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and was too patient afterwards. It also thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse.
n:DSB Bank: DSB Bank was a bank in Amsterdam that collapsed. It is named in a case tied to De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch central bank. The Scheltema committee, set up by finance minister Wouter Bos, reported in June 2010 that the central bank fell seriously short as DSB's supervisor. It missed flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and was too patient afterwards. The committee thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse.
n:AKO Capital: AKO Capital is a company based in London. It is tied to Norges Bank, Norway's central bank, through the hiring of Tangen to run the oil fund. In 2020 the bank's Supervisory Council warned that the hire could carry a risk of breaking laws, rules and guidelines. It said Tangen still appeared to be the main owner of AKO Capital with voting control, despite the bank saying he had cut those ties. It also said the bank had not handled transparency about the applicant list as expected.
n:Sejm of Poland: The Sejm is the lower house of Poland's parliament, based in Warsaw. It is handling the case against Adam Glapiński, president of the National Bank of Poland, the central bank. Ruling coalition members of parliament filed a motion in March 2024 to send him to the State Tribunal, a court that can try senior officials, with eight accusations. They include bond purchases in 2020 and 2021 said to have indirectly financed the deficit by at least 144 billion zloty, and breaching the bank's political neutrality. A committee adopted its report on 9 October 2026, and the Sejm must still decide. The bank calls the accusations entirely groundless.
n:Banco Espírito Santo: Banco Espírito Santo (BES) is a bank based in Lisbon. It is named in a case tied to the Bank of Portugal, the central bank. A 600-page report by a committee the Bank of Portugal itself appointed, with technical support from Boston Consulting Group, pointed to failures in its supervision of BES going back to the start of the previous decade. Information on the Espírito Santo group and on BES's operations in Angola was reportedly not used. The Bank of Portugal twice refused parliament's request for the report.
n:Boston Consulting Group: Boston Consulting Group is a consulting company based in Boston. It gave technical support to a 600-page report by a committee that the Bank of Portugal, the country's central bank, appointed itself. The report pointed to failures in the bank's supervision of Banco Espírito Santo going back to the start of the previous decade. Information on the Espírito Santo group and on the bank's operations in Angola was reportedly not used. The Bank of Portugal twice refused parliament's request for the report.
n:National Bureau of Investigation (Slov: The National Bureau of Investigation is a police investigation unit in Ljubljana, Slovenia. Its investigators filed a second criminal complaint against officials of the Bank of Slovenia, the central bank, alleging abuse of office over the 2013 bank bailout. In that bailout, a 960 million euro bail-in, where investors lose their holdings to rescue a bank, hit about 100,000 junior bondholders and shareholders. A 2016 attempt hit a dead end over procedural errors, and an EU court ruled the European Central Bank's archives were violated. The specialised prosecutor has asked the court to investigate. These are allegations.
n:Specialised State Prosecutor's Office: This is a prosecutor's office in Ljubljana, Slovenia. It has asked a court to investigate officials of the Bank of Slovenia, the central bank, after police filed a second criminal complaint alleging abuse of office over the 2013 bank bailout. In that bailout, a 960 million euro bail-in, where investors lose their holdings to rescue a bank, hit about 100,000 junior bondholders and shareholders. A 2016 attempt hit a dead end over procedural errors, and an EU court ruled the European Central Bank's archives were violated. These are allegations.
n:European Union Rule of Law Mission in: Eulex is the European Union's rule-of-law mission in Kosovo, whose officials can investigate and prosecute cases. It is tied to the Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo through the case of governor Hashim Rexhepi. Eulex law enforcement officials arrested him in July 2010 on suspicion of abusing his official position, accepting bribes, tax evasion, trading in influence and money laundering. A Eulex judge threw out all charges on 12 December. In January 2012, Eulex said its prosecutor would take no further action after it lost an appeal. The case ended without a conviction.
n:MANS (Network for the Affirmation of t: MANS, the Network for the Affirmation of the NGO Sector, is a non-governmental organization based in Podgorica, Montenegro. It is tied to the Central Bank of Montenegro through two claims it made, neither confirmed. It said five payments totaling 4,100 euros went to accounts of relatives of governor Radoje Žugić between January 2017 and April 2018, with no data on their purpose. Žugić reportedly told the daily Dan that he did not act illegally and that aid to relatives of bank employees is not unprecedented. The source reports no finding on the claim.
n:First Bank: First Bank is a bank in Montenegro. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of Montenegro, the country's central bank. In July 2012 the NGO MANS filed reports with Special Prosecutor Djurdjina Ivanovic alleging that First Bank received a 44 million euro state loan in 2008 that it could not repay, and 192.2 million euros from state stock sales in 2009. MANS also alleged that the accused changed banking laws and fired Central Bank administrators so the Central Bank could not supervise First Bank. These are an NGO's reports to the prosecutor, unproven. No charge brought by prosecutors is reported.
n:Otar Partskhaladze: Otar Partskhaladze is a former Prosecutor General of Georgia who was sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury. He is tied to the National Bank of Georgia through its decision to unfreeze assets linked to him, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a Georgian court conviction. Three of the bank's four vice presidents and an advisor submitted resignations over the decision. President Salome Zurabishvili criticized acting president Natia Turnava for reportedly changing the rules unilaterally. No court verdict or official finding is cited.
n:U.S. Department of the Treasury: The U.S. Department of the Treasury is the United States government's finance ministry, based in Washington. It is tied to the National Bank of Georgia through a sanctions dispute. The Treasury had sanctioned Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General of Georgia. The National Bank unfroze assets tied to him, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a Georgian court conviction. Three of its four vice presidents and an advisor submitted resignations over the decision. No court verdict or official finding is cited.
n:Prosecutor's Office of Georgia: The Prosecutor's Office of Georgia, based in Tbilisi, is tied to the National Bank of Georgia through an investigation of one of the bank's officials. It is investigating Council member Nana Keinishvili for possible unlawful involvement in business activities by a public official. The investigation followed complaints from the management of crypto firm Bitexchange LLC, which the National Bank forwarded. The bank had fined Bitexchange. RFE/RL reported the fine at 572 million lari; the bank did not disclose the amount. The investigation was ongoing as of October 2026, and nothing has been proven.
n:Bitexchange LLC: Bitexchange LLC is a crypto firm in Georgia. It is named in a case involving the National Bank of Georgia. The bank fined the company. RFE/RL reported the fine at 572 million lari, and the bank did not disclose the amount. Bitexchange's management complained about Council member Nana Keinishvili, and the National Bank forwarded the complaints. Georgia's Prosecutor's Office is investigating her for possible unlawful involvement in business activities by a public official. The investigation was ongoing as of October 2026, and nothing has been proven.
n:Prosecutor's Office of Bosnia and Herz: The Prosecutor's Office of Bosnia and Herzegovina is based in Sarajevo. It is tied to the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina through a criminal complaint against governor Senad Softić. The complaint accused him of suspected wrongdoing in several cases, including a project to acquire an office building in Pale and a procedure to buy land in Sarajevo. In February 2023 the prosecutor's office said it had opened a case and was verifying the allegations. The central bank said examining allegations is not an investigation and that reports of one were untrue. No finding is reported.
n:Independent Authority Against Corrupti: The Independent Authority Against Corruption of Mongolia (IAAC), based in Ulaanbaatar, is the country's anti-corruption agency. It is tied to the Bank of Mongolia through the arrest of former governor N. Zoljargal on 29 November 2017. IAAC said the case concerned the "Chinggis bond" and a price stabilizing programme, as part of a probe into the bank's 2012-2016 administration. A court released him with a travel ban, and prosecutors had not officially charged him. No later outcome was found.
n:Chingeltei District Criminal Court: The Chingeltei District Criminal Court is a court in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. It is named in a case involving the Bank of Mongolia. The anti-corruption agency IAAC arrested former governor N. Zoljargal on 29 November 2017 and said the case concerned the "Chinggis bond" and a price stabilizing programme, as part of a probe into the bank's 2012-2016 administration. A court released him with a travel ban, and prosecutors had not officially charged him. No later outcome was found.
n:BelAVM: BelAVM is a company in Belarus tied to the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus through an alleged bribe. In December 2016 Belarus's KGB said a directorate head at the National Bank and his deputy were arrested over a bribe, reported as 13,000 dollars, for choosing BelAVM as an equipment supplier. The bribes were allegedly paid in October and November 2016 through intermediaries. Only arrests are reported, with no further charges or verdict, so the allegation is unproven.
n:KGB of Belarus: The KGB of Belarus is the country's security service, based in Minsk. It is tied to the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus through an arrest case. In December 2016 the KGB said a directorate head at the National Bank and his deputy were arrested over a bribe, reported as 13,000 dollars, for choosing the company BelAVM as an equipment supplier. The bribes were allegedly paid in October and November 2016 through intermediaries. Only arrests are reported, with no further charges or verdict, so the allegation is unproven.
n:Blida Criminal Court: The Blida Criminal Court is a court in Blida, Algeria. It is named in a case involving the Bank of Algeria, the Khalifa Bank case. In 2007 the court sentenced former Bank of Algeria governor Abdelwahab Keramane in absentia, meaning without him present, to 20 years in prison. On 7 June 2022 the same court acquitted him. The specific charges are not stated.
n:Capital Markets Authority (Kuwait): The Capital Markets Authority is Kuwait's securities regulator. It is tied to the Central Bank of Kuwait through an unconfirmed press report. The Kuwaiti newspaper Al Jarida, citing unnamed sources, reported that the regulator had decided to refer Governor Mohammad Al Hashel to prosecutors for suspected breach of investment rules over shares in a local bank. He denied it, saying he had never traded shares in a listed company during his senior posts and that buying 2,172 shares in a capital increase did not use inside information. The regulator did not answer Reuters' calls, and no outcome is reported.
n:Al Jarida: Al Jarida is a Kuwaiti newspaper. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of Kuwait. Citing unnamed sources, it reported that the securities regulator had decided to refer Governor Mohammad Al Hashel to prosecutors for suspected breach of investment rules over shares in a local bank. This is unconfirmed. He denied it, saying he had never traded shares in a listed company during his senior posts and that buying 2,172 shares in a capital increase did not use inside information. The regulator did not answer Reuters' calls, and no outcome is reported.
n:Misrata Criminal Court: The Misrata Criminal Court is a court in Misrata, Libya. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of Libya. The court convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize 128 million US dollars and 5 million euros from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion. One received 15 years in prison and a fine of 2.5 million Libyan dinars; the other received 13 years and a fine of 50,000 dinars. The Attorney General's Office reported the ruling in October 2023.
n:Attorney General's Office (Libya): The Attorney General's Office of Libya is tied to the Central Bank of Libya through a theft case. The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize 128 million US dollars and 5 million euros from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion. One received 15 years in prison and a fine of 2.5 million Libyan dinars; the other received 13 years and a fine of 50,000 dinars. The Attorney General's Office reported the ruling in October 2023.
n:Global Witness: Global Witness is an organization based in London. It is tied to the Central Bank of Libya through a report on letters of credit, which are bank guarantees used to pay for imports. Global Witness reported that most Libyan letters of credit enter the international system through ABC International Bank in London, a commercial bank indirectly owned by the central bank and chaired by Governor Saddek Elkaber. It called this a clear conflict of interest, given his authority over letters of credit and anti-money-laundering rules. It built a database of nearly 2.5 billion dollars of letters of credit over 13 weeks in 2020 and said sources described mispricing, laundering and procurement fraud. No official finding of fraud is reported.
n:ABC International Bank PLC: ABC International Bank PLC is a commercial bank in London. It is indirectly owned by the Central Bank of Libya and chaired by Governor Saddek Elkaber. Global Witness reported that most Libyan letters of credit, which are bank guarantees used to pay for imports, enter the international system through it. Global Witness called this a clear conflict of interest, given his authority over letters of credit and anti-money-laundering rules. It built a database of nearly 2.5 billion dollars of letters of credit over 13 weeks in 2020 and said sources described mispricing, laundering and procurement fraud. No official finding of fraud is reported.
n:Attorney-General of Libya: The Attorney-General of Libya is tied to the Central Bank of Libya through a forged banknote complaint. In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature. Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved. No response from al-Hibri and no later outcome are reported, so the accusation is unproven.
n:Prosecutor of the Nouakchott-Ouest tri: The Prosecutor of the Nouakchott-Ouest tribunal is a prosecutor in Nouakchott, Mauritania. It is tied to the Central Bank of Mauritania through a theft case. In July 2020 police under the prosecutor arrested six people, including one bank employee, over foreign currency taken from the central bank. Early reports said about 1 million dollars and later reports 2.4 million dollars, plus 500,000 dollars in counterfeit notes. By March 2021 seven people were in pretrial detention, presumed to have taken about 1 million dollars, and supporters held a sit-in demanding a quick trial. No trial or verdict is reported.
n:Ministry of Justice of Burundi: The Ministry of Justice of Burundi, based in Bujumbura, is tied to the Bank of the Republic of Burundi through a prosecution of its former head. In October 2023 the ministry said dismissed governor Dieudonné Murengerantwari was being prosecuted for passive corruption, money laundering, misappropriation of public property and undermining the national economy. The prosecutor called this description of the facts provisional, and he was being questioned at the time of the report. The charges are unproven.
n:Inspection générale des finances (DR C: The Inspection générale des finances (IGF) is Congo's finance inspectorate, based in Kinshasa. It is tied to the Central Bank of the Congo through an audit report. In April 2021 the IGF called a 43 million dollar transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million dollars in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 dollars. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
n:BGFI Bank RDC: BGFI Bank RDC is a bank in Kinshasa, DR Congo. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of the Congo, which held an account there. In April 2021 Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million dollar transfer from that account to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said BGFI Bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million dollars in the account when the real balance was about 119,000 dollars. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
n:Egal: Egal is a food importer in DR Congo. It is tied to the Central Bank of the Congo as the receiver of a transfer. In April 2021 Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million dollar transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million dollars in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 dollars. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers RDC: PricewaterhouseCoopers RDC is the DR Congo arm of the accounting firm PwC. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of the Congo. In April 2021 Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million dollar transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million dollars in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 dollars. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
n:Belgian federal prosecutor's office: The Belgian federal prosecutor's office, in Brussels, is tied to the Central Bank of the Congo through a money laundering investigation. It opened the investigation into former governor Deogratias Mutombo and five others over hundreds of thousands of dollars allegedly moved through Belgium from DR Congo, with searches in September 2023. As of October 2024 the prosecutor said no suspect had been charged. The matter remains an investigation, and nothing is proven.
n:Central Office for the Suppression of: The Central Office for the Suppression of Corruption is an agency in Brussels, Belgium. It is tied to the Central Bank of the Congo through a money laundering investigation by Belgium's federal prosecutor into former governor Deogratias Mutombo and five others. The case concerns hundreds of thousands of dollars allegedly moved through Belgium from DR Congo, with searches in September 2023. As of October 2024 the prosecutor said no suspect had been charged. Nothing is proven.
n:Janneh Commission: The Janneh Commission is an inquiry based in Banjul, Gambia. It is tied to the Central Bank of The Gambia through its findings on governor Amadou Colley. It found that Colley let former President Jammeh and General Sulayman Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper, the government's formal response to the commission's report, banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
n:Government of The Gambia: The Government of The Gambia, based in Banjul, is tied to the Central Bank of The Gambia through sanctions on a former governor. The Janneh Commission found that governor Amadou Colley let former President Jammeh and General Sulayman Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper, the government's formal response to the commission's report, banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
n:Yahya Jammeh: Yahya Jammeh is a former President of The Gambia. He is tied to the Central Bank of The Gambia through the Janneh Commission, an inquiry. It found that governor Amadou Colley let Jammeh and General Sulayman Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper, the government's formal response, banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
n:Sulayman Badjie: Sulayman Badjie is a general in The Gambia. He is tied to the Central Bank of The Gambia through the Janneh Commission, an inquiry. It found that governor Amadou Colley let former President Jammeh and Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper, the government's formal response, banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
n:Ethiopian anti-corruption officials: Ethiopian anti-corruption officials, based in Addis Ababa, are tied to the National Bank of Ethiopia through a fake gold case. In March 2008 they arrested 26 people after 90 kilos of fake gold were found in the central bank's vaults. Seven of those held were from the National Bank of Ethiopia, four from the Ethiopian Geological Survey and 15 were businessmen and collaborators. The report covers arrests only, not charges or court outcomes.
n:Ethiopian Geological Survey: The Ethiopian Geological Survey is an agency in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It is named in a case involving the National Bank of Ethiopia. In March 2008 anti-corruption officials arrested 26 people after 90 kilos of fake gold were found in the central bank's vaults. Seven of those held were from the National Bank of Ethiopia, four from the Ethiopian Geological Survey and 15 were businessmen and collaborators. n:Rwanda police: Rwanda police, based in Kigali, are tied to the National Bank of Rwanda through a fraud case. The bank lost 63 million Rwandan francs from deposit accounts in early 2014 in a fraud reported to involve bank staff. The bank's ICT director said the suspects manipulated its internal security system before taking the cash. One person was arrested and the file sent to the Prosecutor General, while police said the prime suspect was believed to have fled to Uganda. No verdict is reported.
n:Prosecutor General's office (Rwanda): The Prosecutor General's office of Rwanda, in Kigali, is tied to the National Bank of Rwanda through a fraud case. The bank's ICT director said the suspects manipulated its internal security system before taking the cash. One person was arrested and the file sent to the Prosecutor General, while police said the prime suspect was believed to have fled to Uganda. No verdict is reported.
n:Drug Enforcement Commission (Zambia): The Drug Enforcement Commission of Zambia, based in Lusaka, is tied to the Bank of Zambia through the arrest of one of its employees. In October 2015 it arrested a Bank of Zambia section officer for theft by a public servant and money laundering. He was accused of taking 43,660 US dollars and 20,335 kwacha in cash from his employer between January and September 2015. No court outcome is reported, so the accusation is unproven.
n:Credit Suisse: Credit Suisse is a bank based in Zurich, Switzerland, tied to four central banks. Its links to the Bank of Japan, the Federal Reserve and the Central Bank of Brazil are career moves and paid speeches, not wrongdoing. Seiji Adachi, a Bank of Japan Policy Board member, came from Marusan Securities. Atsushi Mizuno left the Bank of Japan Policy Board to become vice chairman of fixed-income operations in Asia-Pacific at Credit Suisse. Ilan Goldfajn, governor of the Central Bank of Brazil from May 2016 to February 2019, held roles at Itaú Unibanco, Credit Suisse Brazil and the International Monetary Fund. Janet Yellen, Federal Reserve chair until early 2018, was paid by Credit Suisse for speeches or advice after leaving the Fed. Credit Suisse is also named in Mozambique's "hidden debts" case: 2013 letters shown in a US trial indicated the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a 372 million dollar Credit Suisse loan, later 622 million, and Ematum an 850 million dollar loan, part of over 2 billion dollars of hidden debts. Governor Ernesto Gove denied responsibility in 2016; a newssheet reported he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation, which are unproven.
n:VTB: VTB is a bank based in Moscow, Russia. It is named in the "hidden debts" case involving the Bank of Mozambique, Mozambique's central bank. Letters from 2013 presented in a US trial showed the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a 372 million dollar Credit Suisse loan, later 622 million, and Ematum an 850 million dollar loan, part of hidden debts of over 2 billion dollars. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. Carta de Moçambique reported he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation, which are unproven.
n:Anti-Corruption Commission of Bhutan: The Anti-Corruption Commission of Bhutan, based in Thimphu, is tied to the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank, through a case against a former Deputy Governor. An anonymous informer raised it in October 2014. The commission's final findings said he allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. The case was forwarded to the Office of the Attorney General. These are allegations, and no later outcome is reported.
n:Office of the Attorney General of Bhut: The Office of the Attorney General of Bhutan, in Thimphu, is named in a case involving the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the country's central bank. Bhutan's Anti-Corruption Commission said in its final findings that a former Deputy Governor allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. An anonymous informer raised the case in October 2014. The commission forwarded the case to the Attorney General's office. These are allegations, and no later outcome is reported.
n:Daejeon District Court: The Daejeon District Court is a court in Daejeon, South Korea. It is named in a case involving the Bank of Korea. A former currency-exchange employee at the bank's Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the first-in, first-out rule at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 100-won coins from 2018-2019 be issued before 2017 coins. The collector earned about 180 million won selling the coins and gave the employee about 55 million won. The court sentenced the employee to 2 years 6 months in prison, a 1 million won fine and confiscation of about 43.31 million won.
n:Newshub Mediaworks: Newshub Mediaworks is a media company in Auckland, New Zealand. It is tied to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand through a leak. Information on the March Official Cash Rate cut was shared from the bank's media lock-up on 10 March and passed to an economics blogger before the official release. An independent investigation by Deloitte's forensic unit traced the leak to a Newshub Mediaworks reporter. The Reserve Bank ended embargoed lock-ups for news media and analysts.
n:Supreme Court of Thailand: The Supreme Court of Thailand, in Bangkok, is named in a case involving the Bank of Thailand. A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis. On 5 October 2016 the Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case. He was cleared.
n:Supreme Court of Tonga: The Supreme Court of Tonga, in Nuku'alofa, is named in a case involving the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. A Senior Exchange Control Officer at the bank forged a government bond to support another person's New Zealand visa application and asked for 2,500 pa'anga. She pleaded guilty to forgery, knowingly dealing with forged documents and obtaining money by false pretenses, and her employment was terminated. On 21 May 2019 the court gave her a two-year sentence, fully suspended, and ordered 800 pa'anga in compensation.
n:Anti-Corruption Commissioner of Tonga: The Anti-Corruption Commissioner of Tonga, based in Nuku'alofa, is tied to the National Reserve Bank of Tonga through a lawsuit. The commissioner sued the bank and its directors, alleging that a 2024 staff payment (for example 6,600 pa'anga to each of 73 staff) was an unlawful bonus linked to record profit, a breach of trust and misfeasance in public office. The board had described it as a one-off anniversary payout. On 20 November 2025 the Court of Appeal dismissed the proceedings, finding no reasonable cause of action against the bank and that the claim against the directors also failed.
n:Court of Appeal of Tonga: The Court of Appeal of Tonga, in Nuku'alofa, is named in a case involving the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. n:Sandiganbayan: The Sandiganbayan is a court in Quezon City, Philippines. It is named in a case involving Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the country's central bank. After auditing the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga in late 2005, a BSP examiner took consultancy fees from the bank through a third-party firm, collecting 5,000 pesos monthly for a total of 103,500 pesos. The court found he used false pretenses and threatened BSP sanctions. It denied his appeal and affirmed the guilty verdict, with six years and one month to seven years in prison and perpetual disqualification from public office.
n:Prudential Consulting Firm: The Prudential Consulting Firm is a company in the Philippines. It is named in a case involving Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the country's central bank. n:Supreme Court of the Philippines: The Supreme Court of the Philippines, in Manila, is named in a case involving Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the country's central bank. A former officer of the BSP's Supervision and Examination Sector obtained a loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba, Sarangani, Inc. in 2006. The Ombudsman cleared him in 2011 of liability under Section 27(d) in relation to Section 36 of Republic Act 7653. On a petition by the BSP, the Supreme Court reversed the Ombudsman and ordered the filing of criminal charges. Whether they have been filed is not reported.
n:Office of the Ombudsman (Philippines): The Office of the Ombudsman of the Philippines, in Quezon City, is tied to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the country's central bank, through four matters. It cleared a former BSP officer in 2011 over a 2006 loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba; the Supreme Court later reversed it and ordered criminal charges, with filing not reported. It found a Bacolod City branch manager guilty of dishonesty over a 5.955 million peso shortfall, ordered his dismissal and was set to file malversation charges. A January 2021 graft complaint against Governor Benjamin Diokno and six officials over a 1.75 billion peso national ID contract is an unproven allegation with no finding reported. A 2013 complaint over the Allied Bank and Philippine National Bank merger of 9 February 2013 was reported still pending in September 2025.

n:Legislative Council of Hong Kong: The Legislative Council is the lawmaking body of Hong Kong. It is tied to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the city's central bank, as an investigator. The report said Joseph Yam Chi-kwong, the former HKMA chief, should bear "ultimate responsibility" because he headed the banking watchdog at the time. The HKMA replied that the report had not fully taken into account the information it submitted. Some members prepared a minority report.
n:Chris Sinckler: Chris Sinckler was Finance Minister of Barbados. He is tied to the Central Bank of Barbados through the firing of its governor, Delisle Worrell. The government's stated reason was that the board objected to Worrell's reported high-handed manner. Some observers believed the real reason was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money. His January letter said the government must stop taking new money from the bank to pay its bills. The Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him.
n:Anti-Corruption Commission of Myanmar: The Anti-Corruption Commission of Myanmar is a government body based in Naypyitaw, backed by the military junta. It is tied to the Central Bank of Myanmar through the case of former deputy governor Bo Bo Nge. The commission accused him of not collecting tax on a 5 million dollar Open Society deposit and of placing a 350 million dollar loan in a lower-interest account, with alleged losses of 102, 360 and 655 million kyats. A junta court sentenced him to 20 years in prison in December 2022 after a months-long secret trial. He was arrested on the morning of the February 2021 coup. Economist Sean Turnell called him someone "fighting against corruption".
n:Citi: Citi is a bank in New York with ties to several central banks and the Group of Thirty. Catherine L Mann came from Global Chief Economist at Citibank to the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, Michael Saunders from UK economist at Citigroup, and Mervyn King went from Bank of England Governor to senior adviser at Citigroup. The source says it paid former Federal Reserve chair Janet Yellen for speeches, and Stanley Fischer, Governor of the Bank of Israel 2005 to 2013, had been a Citigroup vice chairman. Jane Fraser, Citi's Chair of the Board and CEO, represents it in the Group of Thirty, where central bankers also sit.
n:Brevan Howard Asset Management: Brevan Howard Asset Management is a company in London. Gertjan Vlieghe moved from partner and senior economist there to the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee.
n:Deutsche Bank: Deutsche Bank is a bank in Frankfurt. It is linked to the Bank of England through Gertjan Vlieghe, a Monetary Policy Committee member who came from Brevan Howard Asset Management. The source also says Deutsche Bank hired Alan Greenspan, former Fed chairman, as senior adviser in August 2007.
n:HSBC: HSBC is a bank in London. Michael Saunders went from UK economist at Citigroup to the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee. Jonathan Heath, ratified as Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico on 23 January 2019, had been principal economist at financial institutions including HSBC Mexico.
n:Investec Bank plc: Investec Bank plc is a bank in London. Bradley Fried moved from Chief Executive Officer of Investec Bank plc and co-founder of Grovepoint Capital LLP to Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Grovepoint Capital LLP: Grovepoint Capital LLP is a company in London. Bradley Fried co-founded it and was Chief Executive Officer of Investec Bank plc before becoming Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Lloyds Banking Group: Lloyds Banking Group is a bank in London. David Roberts moved from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag to Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Beazley plc: Beazley plc is a company in London. David Roberts moved from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag to Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Nationwide Building Society: Nationwide Building Society is a building society based in Swindon. David Roberts moved from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag to Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Bawag PSK AG: Bawag PSK AG is a bank in Vienna. David Roberts moved from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag to Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Amadeus Capital Partners: Amadeus Capital Partners is a company in London. Anne Glover moved from investing at Apax Partners and co-founding Amadeus Capital Partners to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Apax Partners: Apax Partners is a company in London. Anne Glover moved from investing at Apax Partners and co-founding Amadeus Capital Partners to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Permira: Permira is a company in London. Diana Noble moved from senior roles at Schroder Ventures (now Permira) to Non-Executive Director and Deputy Chair of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Blackstone: Blackstone is a company in New York. Lord Jitesh Gadhia moved from investment banking at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Baring Brothers: Baring Brothers is a bank in London. Lord Jitesh Gadhia moved from investment banking at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court.
n:BNY: BNY is a bank in New York. Hanneke Smits, Global Head of BNY Investment Management, becomes a Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court from 1 January 2027.
n:Unity Trust Bank: Unity Trust Bank is a bank in Birmingham. Paul Nowak moved from a non-executive role at Unity Trust Bank to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court.
n:Hudson Bay Capital Management: Hudson Bay Capital Management is a company based in Greenwich, United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, through one person's career. Stephen Miran, a Board governor, worked as a senior strategist at Hudson Bay Capital Management, then as chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, before becoming a Fed governor.
n:Farmers & Drovers Bank: Farmers & Drovers Bank is a bank based in Council Grove, United States. It is tied to the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, through one person's career. Michelle W. Bowman, now a Board governor and Vice Chair for Supervision, was a vice president of the bank, then Kansas state bank commissioner, before joining the Fed.
n:PIMCO: PIMCO is an investment company based in Newport Beach, United States. It is tied to the US central bank, the Federal Reserve, mostly through people. Neel Kashkari moved from managing director at PIMCO to president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis. Richard Clarida went from global strategic advisor at PIMCO to Fed vice chairman, then back to PIMCO as managing director. Janet Yellen, former Fed chair, gave paid speeches to PIMCO, according to her disclosures. Raghuram Rajan represents PIMCO in the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers also sit. In May 2020 the New York Fed selected PIMCO as collateral monitor for a 2020 loan program for asset-backed securities.
n:Tudor Investment Corporation: Tudor Investment Corporation is a company based in Stamford, United States. Musalem, now President of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, worked at Tudor, then at the New York Fed, then at Evince Asset Management.
n:Evince Asset Management: Evince Asset Management is a company whose location is not stated; its marker sits at the country level. n:Lehman Brothers: Lehman Brothers is a bank based in New York, United States. It is tied to the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank for the euro, through one person's career. Luis de Guindos, now ECB Vice-President, held chief executive roles at Lehman Brothers and Nomura Securities before joining the ECB.
n:Nomura Securities: Nomura Securities is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan, tied to two central banks through the careers of three people. Luis de Guindos held chief executive roles at Lehman Brothers and Nomura Securities before becoming ECB Vice-President. At the Bank of Japan, Nakagawa Junko moved from chairperson of Nomura Asset Management to the Policy Board, and Takahide Kiuchi moved from Nomura Securities to the Policy Board, where he was nominated as a member.
n:Générale de Banque: Générale de Banque is a bank based in Brussels, Belgium. It is tied to the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank for the euro, through one person's career. n:Fortis Bank: Fortis Bank is a bank based in Brussels, Belgium. It is tied to the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank for the euro, through one person's career. Peter Praet was Chief Economist of Générale de Banque and Fortis Bank before becoming an ECB Executive Board member.
n:Lazard: Lazard is a bank based in New York, United States, tied to two central banks through the careers of two people. n:BBVA: BBVA is a bank based in Bilbao, Spain, tied to three central banks through the careers of three people. n:Société Générale: Société Générale is a bank based in Paris, France. It is tied to the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank for the euro, through one person's career. Lorenzo Bini Smaghi went from ECB Executive Board member to chairman of Societe Generale.
n:Daiwa Securities: Daiwa Securities is a securities firm based in Tokyo. n:Fuji Investment Management: Fuji Investment Management is an investment firm based in Tokyo. n:Deutsche Securities: Deutsche Securities is a securities firm in Tokyo. Adachi Seiji, later a member of the Bank of Japan's Policy Board, moved there in 2004, and on to Marusan Securities in 2013. n:Marusan Securities: Marusan Securities is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Adachi Seiji worked at Marusan Securities before joining the Policy Board.
n:Nomura Asset Management: Nomura Asset Management is a company based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Nakagawa Junko was chairperson of Nomura Asset Management before joining the Policy Board.
n:Industrial Bank of Japan: The Industrial Bank of Japan is a bank based in Tokyo. n:Mizuho Securities: Mizuho Securities is a securities firm based in Tokyo. n:Okasan Securities: Okasan Securities is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Takata Hajime was an executive economist at Okasan Securities before joining the Policy Board.
n:Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Tamura Naoki was an advisor at SMBC and SMFG before joining the Policy Board.
n:Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Tamura Naoki was an advisor at SMBC and SMFG before joining the Policy Board.
n:The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ: The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board member. Suzuki Hitoshi was an advisor at the bank before joining the Policy Board.

n:The Toronto-Dominion Bank: The Toronto-Dominion Bank is a bank based in Toronto, Canada. n:Crédit Agricole Indosuez: Crédit Agricole Indosuez is a bank based in Paris, France. n:Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities: Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities is a bank based in Tokyo, Japan. It is tied to the Bank of Japan, Japan's central bank, through the employment of a Policy Board nominee. Takehiro Sato moved from the firm to a nomination to the Policy Board.
n:Ombudsman of Vanuatu: The Ombudsman of Vanuatu is the national office that investigates complaints about public officials. The report found that Governor Samson Ngwele improperly executed ten bank guarantees totalling 100 million US dollars, without Board approval and under pressure from Finance Minister Barak Sope. It found this breached the Reserve Bank Act and the Leadership Code. The guarantees went to Peter Harold Swanson for a "Trading Programme" that the Ombudsman called a scam, and were still in circulation at the time of the report.
